## P4 - No test covers the fractional-speed guard in `PortSpeed.UnmarshalYAML`

**Location:** [nodes/mikrotik&#95;chr/port&#95;speeds.go:36-48](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ffb224edfdf561661adac339b26ce3bc693ad5b3/nodes/mikrotik_chr/port_speeds.go#L36-L48)

**Problem:** `UnmarshalYAML` on `PortSpeed` exists solely to reject a fractional `speed` before `yaml.v2` silently truncates it into the `int` field, which would accept `speed: 1000.5` as `1000` with no error. `TestDecodePortSpeeds` in [`port_speeds_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ffb224edfdf561661adac339b26ce3bc693ad5b3/nodes/mikrotik_chr/port_speeds_test.go#L1-L1) covers a numeric `port`, a range, a string `speed` &#40;`1G`&#41;, and an unknown field, but has no case with a fractional `speed`, so this guard is untested.

**Trigger:** A future refactor of the decode path, such as dropping `UnmarshalYAML`, switching the second decode pass to a different mode, or changing `Speed` to a float-typed intermediate, would let `speed: 1000.5` decode to `1000` without any test failing.

**Impact:** Silent acceptance of a typo like `speed: 2.5` &#40;intended as 2.5 Gbit/s&#41; as 2 Mb/s, reintroducing exactly the truncation the guard was written to prevent. The likelihood is low, but the guard&#39;s entire purpose is this one edge, so nothing currently pins it.

**Suggested correction:** Add one case to the table in `TestDecodePortSpeeds`&#58; `"speed-fraction": {yaml: "- port: 2\n  speed: 1000.5\n", errText: "whole number"}`. This is the smallest useful check; the error text matches `speed must be a whole number of Mb/s, got 1000.5` produced at [`port_speeds.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ffb224edfdf561661adac339b26ce3bc693ad5b3/nodes/mikrotik_chr/port_speeds.go#L1-L1) line 43.


## Coverage

- Source-only review; all changed paths and tests were read but not executed.
- Decode/`Init` paths traced&#58; `DecodeKindSpecificConfig` always yields `*KindSpecificConfig`, so `kindSpecificConfig.Of(n.Cfg)` cannot panic; `createNodeCfg` returns decode errors before `Init`; the reconcile `createNodeConfig` is only used for `ComputeDiff`; `AddPlaceholderNode` only runs with placeholder kinds; `MergeStringMaps` keeps `n.Cfg.Env` non-nil.
- Validation verified&#58; `portRange` rejects `ether1`, over-limit ports, descending/half/non-numeric/zero-padded ranges, and duplicates; speeds bounded to `1..math.MaxInt32`; `Init` always overwrites `CHR_PORT_SPEEDS` &#40;test `replaces-env`&#41;.
- Launcher verified&#58; `data_nic_speed` exact-match with10000 default; `data_nic_device` appends `speed=...,duplex=full` on both PCI layouts; re-plug via `device_add $(data_nic_device ...)` keeps the `speed`; per-port LACP `group_fwd_mask` writes fall back to `log`; `log()` defined before first use; O&#40;ports x pairs&#41; loop is negligible at the 63-port limit.
- Schema verified&#58; `port-speeds` node property, node if/then, `kinds.mikrotik_chr` entry, and new `kind-specific-config-mikrotik_chr` definition are mutually consistent; every other kind definition including `kind-specific-config-other` gained the `port-speeds` exclusion; `defaults` accepting all keys is a pre-existing pattern.
- Docs verified&#58; precedence/`port-speeds: []` reset semantics match `GetNodeKindSpecificConfig`, `#port-speed` anchor matches the schema link, arch limits and ARM64 TCG caveat documented; no stale references in [`nodes.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ffb224edfdf561661adac339b26ce3bc693ad5b3/docs/manual/nodes.md#L1-L1) or `kinds/index.md`.
- `yaml.v2` edges verified&#58; `int` and string `port` both decode; `1G`, `26.0`, hex rejected; `0.5e3` decodes to 500; unknown fields rejected by the strict pass &#40;tested&#41;.
- Not verifiable from source&#58; `RouterOS` 802.3ad full-duplex requirement and ARM64 TCG 22-NIC observation are author-reported and documented as such; the image&#39;s QEMU version support for `speed`/`duplex` could not be confirmed without running the image.

72: +The container interface `ethN` is RouterOS `ether(N+1)`, also when links leave gaps: a link on `eth12` alone still lands on `ether13`, with `ether2` to `ether12` present and unlinked. Interface MTU follows the link MTU, and LLDP and LACP frames are forwarded, so `/ip neighbor` shows the peers and 802.3ad bonds can form.
73:  
74:  On AMD64, data NICs are placed behind PCI bridges rather than sharing the default PC's root bus with all other devices. This removes the default layout's limit of 29 total Ethernet interfaces (management plus 28 data ports), so links can use `ether30` and higher without a custom launcher. ARM64 still uses a single PCI bus on the `virt` machine, shared with the disk and the management NIC; the PCI-bridge expansion applies only to AMD64.
75:  
76:  /// admonition
77:      type: warning
78: -The highest interface depends on the architecture, and larger indices are rejected during deployment:
79: +Containerlab checks the highest interface index against these architecture limits:
80:  
81:  * AMD64: `eth63` / `ether64`, the highest port tested. More interfaces exhaust the guest's interrupt vectors (with the default single vCPU) and, from about 200, the virtual PC firmware's PCI address space, which stops the VM before RouterOS boots.
82: -* ARM64: `eth29` / `ether30`, the last data port that fits on the `virt` machine's PCI bus.
83: +* ARM64: `eth29` / `ether30`, the last data port that fits on the `virt` machine's PCI bus. RouterOS may stop earlier. With QEMU software emulation (TCG), RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.26beta7 brought up only 22 data NICs, through `eth22` / `ether23`. A topology that links `ether24` or higher can pass validation but leave the node unhealthy. Keep links at or below `ether23` on these ARM64 setups.
84:  
85:  The check uses the architecture of the containerlab binary, which matches the image's except in emulated setups.
86:  ///
87:  
88:  With more than about 30 data ports, RouterOS can reject a NIC while it boots, and the interface does not appear. The launcher checks that RouterOS has an interface for every data NIC and re-plugs the missing ones before the node reports ready; RouterOS keeps their configuration. It checks again after RouterOS reboots itself (for example with `/system reboot`), when the container keeps running. If a NIC is still missing, the launcher logs `data NIC check FAILED` and the node is not healthy. The node is also not healthy while RouterOS does not answer within `CHR_BOOT_WAIT` after such a reboot.
89:  
90:  Sparse interface numbering also consumes VM resources for the intervening ports; memory defaults scale with the highest index, not just the number of links.
91:  
92: +### Port speed
93: +
94: +Data interfaces report 10 Gbit/s and full duplex by default, matching a container veth. RouterOS needs full-duplex member links for an 802.3ad bond. Each data bridge must also forward LACP frames between the container veth and the QEMU tap so RouterOS and its peer can negotiate the bond.
95: +
96: +To model the ports of a real device, set `port-speeds`, a [kind-specific config](../nodes.md#kind-specific-config) key. Each entry sets the speed in Mb/s for one data port or an inclusive range: `port` is the RouterOS port number (`2` for `ether2`) or a range such as `2..25`. Ports that are not listed keep 10 Gbit/s. The speed is what RouterOS shows; it does not limit traffic.
97: +
98: +Set `port-speeds` in a [group](../topo-def-file.md#groups) to describe a device model once and reuse it. A device's own management port is `ether1`, the node's management interface. Assign data ports starting at `ether2`. The CRS518 example puts the 25G ports first. A QSFP cage counts as one port, as RouterOS runs the full 40G or 100G link on its first lane.
99: +
100: +```yaml
101: +name: chr-port-speeds
102: +topology:
103: +  groups:
104: +    crs317-1g-16s: # 16 x 10G SFP+
105: +      kind: mikrotik_chr
106: +      image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5
107: +      port-speeds:
108: +        - port: 2..17
109: +          speed: 10000
110: +    crs518-16xs-2xq: # 16 x 25G SFP28, 2 x 100G QSFP28
111: +      kind: mikrotik_chr
112: +      image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5
113: +      port-speeds:
114: +        - port: 2..17
115: +          speed: 25000
116: +        - port: 18..19
117: +          speed: 100000
118: +  nodes:
119: +    access1:
120: +      group: crs317-1g-16s
121: +    core1:
122: +      group: crs518-16xs-2xq
123: +  links:
124: +    - endpoints: ["access1:ether16", "core1:ether2"]
125: +    - endpoints: ["access1:ether17", "core1:ether19"]
126: +```
127: +
128: +A node that sets `port-speeds` itself replaces the group's list. Use `port-speeds: []` to restore the defaults. Containerlab rejects `ether1`, a port above the [architecture limit](#interface-naming), a duplicate port, or a speed outside 1 to 2147483647 Mb/s. A group may list ports without links. The container log lists the speed of each data NIC the node creates.

294: +func TestDataNICSpeed(t *testing.T) {
295: +	tests := map[string]struct {

302: +		"listed-port":     {speeds: "2:1000 3:1000", index: 1, want: "1000"},
303: +		"last-listed":     {speeds: "2:25000 18:100000 19:100000", index: 18, want: "100000"},
304: +		"unlisted-port":   {speeds: "2:1000 26:10000", index: 2, want: "10000"},
305: +		"no-prefix-match": {speeds: "12:1000", index: 1, want: "10000"},
306: +		"highest-port":    {speeds: "64:100000", index: 63, want: "100000"},

313: +				fn+"data_nic_speed \"$1\"", "chr-launch-test", fmt.Sprint(tc.index))
314: +			// Only the test's variables: a CHR_PORT_SPEEDS of the host must not leak in.
315: +			cmd.Env = []string{"PATH=/usr/bin:/bin", "CHR_PORT_SPEEDS=" + tc.speeds}
316: +			out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()

408: diff --git a/nodes/mikrotik_chr/port_speeds.go b/nodes/mikrotik_chr/port_speeds.go
409: new file mode 100644
410: index 0000000..8740f79
411: --- /dev/null
412: +++ b/nodes/mikrotik_chr/port_speeds.go
413: @@ -0,0 +1,107 @@
414: +package mikrotik_chr
415: +
416: +import (
417: +	"fmt"
418: +	"maps"
419: +	"math"
420: +	"slices"
421: +	"strconv"
422: +	"strings"
423: +
424: +	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
425: +)
426: +
427: +const (
428: +	// portSpeedsEnv hands the port speeds to the launcher as "<port>:<Mb/s>" pairs, e.g.
429: +	// "2:1000 3:1000". The kind always sets it, so only validated speeds reach QEMU.
430: +	portSpeedsEnv = "CHR_PORT_SPEEDS"
431: +	// maxPortSpeed is the highest speed QEMU's virtio-net accepts (an int32, in Mb/s).
432: +	maxPortSpeed = math.MaxInt32
433: +)
434: +
435: +// KindSpecificConfig is the mikrotik_chr kind-specific config, set as keys on the node
436: +// definition.
437: +type KindSpecificConfig struct {
438: +	// PortSpeeds sets the speed that data ports report, for one port or an inclusive range.
439: +	PortSpeeds []PortSpeed `yaml:"port-speeds,omitempty" json:"port-speeds,omitempty"`
440: +}
441: +
442: +// PortSpeed sets the speed in Mb/s that data ports report. Port is a RouterOS port number, 2 for
443: +// ether2, or an inclusive range such as 2..25.
444: +type PortSpeed struct {
445: +	Port  string `yaml:"port"  json:"port"`
446: +	Speed int    `yaml:"speed" json:"speed"`
447: +}
448: +
449: +// UnmarshalYAML checks for a fraction before yaml.v2 can truncate it to an int.
450: +func (p *PortSpeed) UnmarshalYAML(unmarshal func(any) error) error {
451: +	var raw map[string]any
452: +	if err := unmarshal(&raw); err != nil {
453: +		return err
454: +	}
455: +	if speed, ok := raw["speed"].(float64); ok && speed != math.Trunc(speed) {
456: +		return fmt.Errorf("speed must be a whole number of Mb/s, got %v", speed)
457: +	}
458: +
459: +	type plainPortSpeed PortSpeed
460: +	return unmarshal((*plainPortSpeed)(p))
461: +}
462: +
463: +var kindSpecificConfig clabnodes.KindSpecificConfigSpec[KindSpecificConfig]
464: +
465: +// portSpeeds validates the port-speeds key and returns its "<port>:<Mb/s>" pairs in port order.
466: +// lastPort is the highest data port the NIC layout holds (ether30 on arm64, ether64 on amd64).
467: +// A port without a link is allowed: one port-speeds list in a group can serve nodes that do not
468: +// link every port.
469: +func portSpeeds(cfg *KindSpecificConfig, lastPort int) (string, error) {
470: +	speeds := map[int]int{}
471: +
472: +	for _, ps := range cfg.PortSpeeds {
473: +		first, last, err := portRange(ps.Port, lastPort)
474: +		if err != nil {
475: +			return "", err
476: +		}
477: +		if ps.Speed < 1 || ps.Speed > maxPortSpeed {
478: +			return "", fmt.Errorf(
479: +				"port-speeds: port %q: speed must be between 1 and %d Mb/s, got %d",
480: +				ps.Port, maxPortSpeed, ps.Speed,
481: +			)
482: +		}
483: +		for p := first; p <= last; p++ {
484: +			if _, ok := speeds[p]; ok {
485: +				return "", fmt.Errorf("port-speeds: ether%d is set more than once", p)
486: +			}
487: +			speeds[p] = ps.Speed
488: +		}
489: +	}
490: +
491: +	pairs := make([]string, 0, len(speeds))
492: +	for _, p := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(speeds)) {
493: +		pairs = append(pairs, fmt.Sprintf("%d:%d", p, speeds[p]))
494: +	}
495: +
496: +	return strings.Join(pairs, " "), nil
497: +}
498: +
499: +// portRange parses a data port number or an ascending inclusive range such as 2..25, within
500: +// ether2 to ether<lastPort>.
501: +func portRange(port string, lastPort int) (int, int, error) {
502: +	firstText, lastText, isRange := strings.Cut(port, "..")
503: +	if !isRange {
504: +		lastText = firstText
505: +	}
506: +
507: +	first, firstErr := strconv.Atoi(firstText)
508: +	last, lastErr := strconv.Atoi(lastText)
509: +	if firstErr != nil || lastErr != nil ||
510: +		strconv.Itoa(first) != firstText || strconv.Itoa(last) != lastText ||
511: +		first < InterfaceOffset || last < first || last > lastPort {
512: +		return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf(
513: +			"port-speeds: port %q must be a port number or an ascending range within %d..%d "+
514: +				"(ether%d to ether%d)",
515: +			port, InterfaceOffset, lastPort, InterfaceOffset, lastPort,
516: +		)
517: +	}
518: +
519: +	return first, last, nil
520: +}

670: +// TestDecodePortSpeeds decodes the key from YAML the way a topology sets it: a single port may be
671: +// written as a number, a range as a string, and a speed must be a number.
672: +func TestDecodePortSpeeds(t *testing.T) {
673: +	tests := map[string]struct {
674: +		yaml    string
675: +		want    []PortSpeed
676: +		errText string
677: +	}{
678: +		"number-and-range": {
679: +			yaml: "- port: 26\n  speed: 10000\n- port: 2..25\n  speed: 1000\n",
680: +			want: []PortSpeed{{Port: "26", Speed: 10000}, {Port: "2..25", Speed: 1000}},
681: +		},
682: +		"speed-with-unit": {
683: +			yaml:    "- port: 2\n  speed: 1G\n",
684: +			errText: `invalid value for key "port-speeds" (set in nodes.r1)`,
685: +		},
686: +		"unknown-field": {
687: +			yaml:    "- port: 2\n  speed: 1000\n  duplex: half\n",
688: +			errText: "field duplex not found",
689: +		},
690: +	}
691: +
692: +	registry := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistry()
693: +	Register(registry)
694: +
695: +	for name, tc := range tests {
696: +		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
697: +			var value any
698: +			if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(tc.yaml), &value); err != nil {
699: +				t.Fatal(err)
700: +			}
701: +			got, err := clabnodes.DecodeKindSpecificConfig(
702: +				registry.Kind("mikrotik_chr"),
703: +				"r1",
704: +				"mikrotik_chr",
705: +				[]clabtypes.KindSpecificConfigEntry{
706: +					{Key: "port-speeds", Value: value, From: "nodes.r1"},
707: +				},
708: +			)
709: +			if tc.errText != "" {
710: +				if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.errText) {
711: +					t.Fatalf("decode = %v, want an error containing %q", err, tc.errText)
712: +				}
713: +
714: +				return
715: +			}
716: +			if err != nil {
717: +				t.Fatal(err)
718: +			}
719: +			cfg, ok := got.(*KindSpecificConfig)
720: +			if !ok {
721: +				t.Fatalf("decoded %T, want *KindSpecificConfig", got)
722: +			}
723: +			if len(cfg.PortSpeeds) != len(tc.want) {
724: +				t.Fatalf("PortSpeeds = %v, want %v", cfg.PortSpeeds, tc.want)
725: +			}

RouterOS needs full-duplex member links for an 802.3ad bond. Each data bridge must also forward LACP frames between the container veth and the QEMU tap so RouterOS and its peer can negotiate the bond.\n95: +\n96: +To model the ports of a real device, set `port-speeds`, a [kind-specific config](../nodes.md#kind-specific-config) key. The speed is what RouterOS shows; it does not limit traffic.\n97: +\n98: +Set `port-speeds` in a [group](../topo-def-file.md#groups) to describe a device model once and reuse it. Interface MTU follows the link MTU, and LLDP frames are forwarded, so `/ip neighbor` shows the peers.\n+The container interface `ethN` is RouterOS `ether(N+1)`, also when links leave gaps: a link on `eth12` alone still lands on `ether13`, with `ether2` to `ether12` present and unlinked. Interface MTU follows the link MTU, and LLDP and LACP frames are forwarded, so `/ip neighbor` shows the peers and 802.3ad bonds can form.\n \n On AMD64, data NICs are placed behind PCI bridges rather than sharing the default PC's root bus with all other devices. This removes the default layout's limit of 29 total Ethernet interfaces (management plus 28 data ports), so links can use `ether30` and higher without a custom launcher. ARM64 still uses a single PCI bus on the `virt` machine, shared with the disk and the management NIC; the PCI-bridge expansion applies only to AMD64.\n \n /// admonition\n     type: warning\n-The highest interface depends on the architecture, and larger indices are rejected during deployment:\n+Containerlab checks the highest interface index against these architecture limits:\n \n * AMD64: `eth63` / `ether64`, the highest port tested. More interfaces exhaust the guest's interrupt vectors (with the default single vCPU) and, from about 200, the virtual PC firmware's PCI address space, which stops the VM before RouterOS boots.\n-* ARM64: `eth29` / `ether30`, the last data port that fits on the `virt` machine's PCI bus.\n+* ARM64: `eth29` / `ether30`, the last data port that fits on the `virt` machine's PCI bus. RouterOS may stop earlier. With QEMU software emulation (TCG), RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.26beta7 brought up only 22 data NICs, through `eth22` / `ether23`. A topology that links `ether24` or higher can pass validation but leave the node unhealthy. Keep links at or below `ether23` on these ARM64 setups.\n \n The check uses the architecture of the containerlab binary, which matches the image's except in emulated setups.\n ///\n \n With more than about 30 data ports, RouterOS can reject a NIC while it boots, and the interface does not appear. The launcher checks that RouterOS has an interface for every data NIC and re-plugs the missing ones before the node reports ready; RouterOS keeps their configuration. It checks again after RouterOS reboots itself (for example with `/system reboot`), when the container keeps running. If a NIC is still missing, the launcher logs `data NIC check FAILED` and the node is not healthy. The node is also not healthy while RouterOS does not answer within `CHR_BOOT_WAIT` after such a reboot.\n \n Sparse interface numbering also consumes VM resources for the intervening ports; memory defaults scale with the highest index, not just the number of links.\n \n+### Port speed\n+\n+Data interfaces report 10 Gbit/s and full duplex by default, matching a container veth. RouterOS needs full-duplex member links for an 802.3ad bond. Each data bridge must also forward LACP frames between the container veth and the QEMU tap so RouterOS and its peer can negotiate the bond.\n+\n+To model the ports of a real device, set `port-speeds`, a [kind-specific config](../nodes.md#kind-specific-config) key. Each entry sets the speed in Mb/s for one data port or an inclusive range: `port` is the RouterOS port number (`2` for `ether2`) or a range such as `2..25`. Ports that are not listed keep 10 Gbit/s. The speed is what RouterOS shows; it does not limit traffic.\n+\n+Set `port-speeds` in a [group](../topo-def-file.md#groups) to describe a device model once and reuse it. A device's own management port is `ether1`, the node's management interface. Assign data ports starting at `ether2`. The CRS518 example puts the 25G ports first. A QSFP cage counts as one port, as RouterOS runs the full 40G or 100G link on its first lane.\n+\n+```yaml\n+name: chr-port-speeds\n+topology:\n+  groups:\n+    crs317-1g-16s: # 16 x 10G SFP+\n+      kind: mikrotik_chr\n+      image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5\n+      port-speeds:\n+        - port: 2..17\n+          speed: 10000\n+    crs518-16xs-2xq: # 16 x 25G SFP28, 2 x 100G QSFP28\n+      kind: mikrotik_chr\n+      image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5\n+      port-speeds:\n+        - port: 2..17\n+          speed: 25000\n+        - port: 18..19\n+          speed: 100000\n+  nodes:\n+    access1:\n+      group: crs317-1g-16s\n+    core1:\n+      group: crs518-16xs-2xq\n+  links:\n+    - endpoints: [\"access1:ether16\", \"core1:ether2\"]\n+    - endpoints: [\"access1:ether17\", \"core1:ether19\"]\n+```\n+\n+A node that sets `port-speeds` itself replaces the group's list. Use `port-speeds: []` to restore the defaults. Containerlab rejects `ether1`, a port above the [architecture limit](#interface-naming), a duplicate port, or a speed outside 1 to 2147483647 Mb/s. A group may list ports without links. The container log lists the speed of each data NIC the node creates.\n+\n ## Node configuration\n \n -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes boot with the default CHR configuration plus the credentials, the identity (set to the node name) and the management setup described below.\n \n ### Startup configuration\ndiff --git a/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh b/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh\nindex dd96d9e..6de90f7 100644\n--- a/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh\n+++ b/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh\n@@ -17,12 +17,12 @@\n #      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS\n #      ether1. NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so\n+#      container ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps\n #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is\n #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,\n #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return\n #      path in its own VRF (`mgmt`, below), then fetches\n #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)\n@@ -206,25 +206,38 @@ check_nic_index() { # check_nic_index <max-index>: reject indices beyond the NIC\n         log \"at most 29 data NICs fit without PCI bridges (eth29 / ether30); index $1 leaves no PCI slot for the disk\"\n         return 1\n     fi\n }\n \n+data_nic_speed() { # data_nic_speed <index>: the data NIC's speed in Mb/s\n+    # The kind writes the validated port-speeds key to CHR_PORT_SPEEDS as\n+    # \"<port>:<Mb/s>\" pairs; data NIC <index> is ether<index+1>. Other ports\n+    # report 10G, the speed a container veth reports.\n+    for _pair in ${CHR_PORT_SPEEDS:-}; do\n+        [ \"${_pair%%:*}\" = \"$(( $1 + 1 ))\" ] && { printf '%s' \"${_pair#*:}\"; return; 1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

1: package mikrotik_chr
2: 
3: import (
4: 	"fmt"
5: 	"maps"
6: 	"math"
7: 	"slices"
8: 	"strconv"
9: 	"strings"
10: 
11: 	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
12: )
13: 
14: const (
15: 	// portSpeedsEnv hands the port speeds to the launcher as "<port>:<Mb/s>" pairs, e.g.
16: 	// "2:1000 3:1000". The kind always sets it, so only validated speeds reach QEMU.
17: 	portSpeedsEnv = "CHR_PORT_SPEEDS"
18: 	// maxPortSpeed is the highest speed QEMU's virtio-net accepts (an int32, in Mb/s).
19: 	maxPortSpeed = math.MaxInt32
20: )
21: 
22: // KindSpecificConfig is the mikrotik_chr kind-specific config, set as keys on the node
23: // definition.
24: type KindSpecificConfig struct {
25: 	// PortSpeeds sets the speed that data ports report, for one port or an inclusive range.
26: 	PortSpeeds []PortSpeed `yaml:"port-speeds,omitempty" json:"port-speeds,omitempty"`
27: }
28: 
29: // PortSpeed sets the speed in Mb/s that data ports report. Port is a RouterOS port number, 2 for
30: // ether2, or an inclusive range such as 2..25.
31: type PortSpeed struct {
32: 	Port  string `yaml:"port"  json:"port"`
33: 	Speed int    `yaml:"speed" json:"speed"`
34: }
35: 
36: // UnmarshalYAML checks for a fraction before yaml.v2 can truncate it to an int.
37: func (p *PortSpeed) UnmarshalYAML(unmarshal func(any) error) error {
38: 	var raw map[string]any
39: 	if err := unmarshal(&raw); err != nil {
40: 		return err
41: 	}
42: 	if speed, ok := raw["speed"].(float64); ok && speed != math.Trunc(speed) {
43: 		return fmt.Errorf("speed must be a whole number of Mb/s, got %v", speed)
44: 	}
45: 
46: 	type plainPortSpeed PortSpeed
47: 	return unmarshal((*plainPortSpeed)(p))
48: }
49: 
50: var kindSpecificConfig clabnodes.KindSpecificConfigSpec[KindSpecificConfig]
51: 
52: // portSpeeds validates the port-speeds key and returns its "<port>:<Mb/s>" pairs in port order.
53: // lastPort is the highest data port the NIC layout holds (ether30 on arm64, ether64 on amd64).
54: // A port without a link is allowed: one port-speeds list in a group can serve nodes that do not
55: // link every port.
56: func portSpeeds(cfg *KindSpecificConfig, lastPort int) (string, error) {
57: 	speeds := map[int]int{}
58: 
59: 	for _, ps := range cfg.PortSpeeds {
60: 		first, last, err := portRange(ps.Port, lastPort)
61: 		if err != nil {
62: 			return "", err
63: 		}
64: 		if ps.Speed < 1 || ps.Speed > maxPortSpeed {
65: 			return "", fmt.Errorf(
66: 				"port-speeds: port %q: speed must be between 1 and %d Mb/s, got %d",
67: 				ps.Port, maxPortSpeed, ps.Speed,
68: 			)
69: 		}
70: 		for p := first; p <= last; p++ {
71: 			if _, ok := speeds[p]; ok {
72: 				return "", fmt.Errorf("port-speeds: ether%d is set more than once", p)
73: 			}
74: 			speeds[p] = ps.Speed
75: 		}
76: 	}
77: 
78: 	pairs := make([]string, 0, len(speeds))
79: 	for _, p := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(speeds)) {
80: 		pairs = append(pairs, fmt.Sprintf("%d:%d", p, speeds[p]))
81: 	}
82: 
83: 	return strings.Join(pairs, " "), nil
84: }
85: 
86: // portRange parses a data port number or an ascending inclusive range such as 2..25, within
87: // ether2 to ether<lastPort>.
88: func portRange(port string, lastPort int) (int, int, error) {
89: 	firstText, lastText, isRange := strings.Cut(port, "..")
90: 	if !isRange {
91: 		lastText = firstText
92: 	}
93: 
94: 	first, firstErr := strconv.Atoi(firstText)
95: 	last, lastErr := strconv.Atoi(lastText)
96: 	if firstErr != nil || lastErr != nil ||
97: 		strconv.Itoa(first) != firstText || strconv.Itoa(last) != lastText ||
98: 		first < InterfaceOffset || last < first || last > lastPort {
99: 		return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf(
100: 			"port-speeds: port %q must be a port number or an ascending range within %d..%d "+
101: 				"(ether%d to ether%d)",
102: 			port, InterfaceOffset, lastPort, InterfaceOffset, lastPort,
103: 		)
104: 	}
105: 
106: 	return first, last, nil
107: }

(End of file - total 107 lines)

1: // Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs
2: // Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
3: // SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
4: 
5: // Package mikrotik_chr runs MikroTik RouterOS CHR from the official mikrotik/chr image.
6: //
7: // The image is MikroTik's own distribution (Alpine + qemu + the CHR disk) and is used
8: // unmodified: the kind writes chr-launch.sh into the node's lab directory, bind-mounts it
9: // read-only and sets it as the entrypoint in place of the image's /start.sh, which is not
10: // orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116, #3464).
11: package mikrotik_chr
12: 
13: import (
14: 	"context"
15: 	_ "embed"
16: 	"errors"
17: 	"fmt"
18: 	"net"
19: 	"os"
20: 	"path"
21: 	"path/filepath"
22: 	"regexp"
23: 	"runtime"
24: 	"slices"
25: 	"strconv"
26: 	"strings"
27: 
28: 	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
29: 	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
30: 	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
31: 	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
32: )
33: 
34: var (
35: 	kindNames          = []string{"mikrotik_chr"}
36: 	defaultCredentials = clabnodes.NewCredentials("admin", "admin")
37: 
38: 	InterfaceRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`ether(?P<port>\d+)`)
39: 	InterfaceOffset = 2
40: 	InterfaceHelp   = "etherX (where X >= 2) or ethX (where X >= 1)"
41: 
42: 	//go:embed chr-launch.sh
43: 	launcherScript []byte
44: )
45: 
46: const (
47: 	configDirName   = "ftpboot"
48: 	startupCfgFName = "config.auto.rsc"
49: 
50: 	launcherFName = "chr-launch.sh"
51: 	launcherPath  = "/chr-launch.sh"
52: 
53: 	// readyFile is written by the launcher once RouterOS accepted the credentials and the
54: 	// startup config, and removed at every container start.
55: 	readyFile = "/.chr-launch-ready"
56: 
57: 	// mgmtComment tags every management object the launcher creates in RouterOS.
58: 	mgmtComment = "clab-mgmt"
59: 
60: 	// amd64's tested PCI-bridge layout. Beyond it the guest runs out of interrupt
61: 	// vectors (about 100 NICs per vCPU) and SeaBIOS out of PCI I/O space (8 bridges).
62: 	maxDataNICIndex = 63
63: 	// arm64's virt machine gets no PCI bridges: its single bus holds the disk, the
64: 	// management NIC and at most 29 data NICs before QEMU runs out of slots.
65: 	maxDataNICIndexARM64 = 29
66: 
67: 	// the launcher's CHR_INTF_WAIT and CHR_BOOT_WAIT defaults, and the time its config
68: 	// fetch and gateway check add, in seconds.
69: 	defaultIntfWait  = 60
70: 	defaultBootWait  = 300
71: 	startPeriodSlack = 90
72: 	// the launcher's wait for the interface list to settle and its re-plug rounds, in seconds.
73: 	replugWait = 180
74: 
75: 	scrapliPlatformName = "mikrotik_routeros" //nolint: misspell
76: )
77: 
78: // Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
79: func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
80: 	platformAttrs := &clabnodes.PlatformAttrs{
81: 		ScrapliPlatformName: scrapliPlatformName,
82: 	}
83: 
84: 	nrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(defaultCredentials, nil, platformAttrs).
85: 		WithKindSpecificConfig(kindSpecificConfig)
86: 
87: 	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
88: 		return new(mikrotikCHR)
89: 	}, nrea)
90: }
91: 
92: type mikrotikCHR struct {
93: 	clabnodes.VRNode
94: 	// goarch selects the NIC layout the interface limit is checked against. The
95: 	// containerlab binary's architecture matches the image's outside emulated setups.
96: 	goarch string
97: }
98: 
99: func (n *mikrotikCHR) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
100: 	n.VRNode = *clabnodes.NewVRNode(n, defaultCredentials, scrapliPlatformName)
101: 	n.ConfigDirName = configDirName
102: 	n.StartupCfgFName = startupCfgFName
103: 	// The image's qemu falls back to TCG emulation without /dev/kvm: KVM makes the boot
104: 	// fast but is not required.
105: 	n.HostRequirements.VirtRequired = false
106: 
107: 	n.Cfg = cfg
108: 	for _, o := range opts {
109: 		o(n)
110: 	}
111: 
112: 	// Credentials travel as env, not on the command line, so a password needs no quoting.
113: 	defEnv := map[string]string{
114: 		"USERNAME": n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
115: 		"PASSWORD": n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
116: 	}
117: 	n.Cfg.Env = clabutils.MergeStringMaps(defEnv, n.Cfg.Env)
118: 
119: 	n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds,
120: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, configDirName), ":/ftpboot"),
121: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName), ":", launcherPath, ":ro"),
122: 	)
123: 
124: 	if n.Cfg.Entrypoint == "" {
125: 		n.Cfg.Entrypoint = "/bin/sh " + launcherPath
126: 	}
127: 	n.Cfg.Cmd = fmt.Sprintf("--hostname %s", n.Cfg.ShortName)
128: 
129: 	if n.Cfg.Healthcheck == nil {
130: 		n.Cfg.Healthcheck = &clabtypes.HealthcheckConfig{
131: 			Test:        []string{"CMD-SHELL", "test -f " + readyFile},
132: 			Interval:    5,
133: 			Timeout:     3,
134: 			Retries:     3,
135: 			StartPeriod: startPeriod(n.Cfg.Env),
136: 		}
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	n.InterfaceRegexp = InterfaceRegexp
140: 	n.InterfaceOffset = InterfaceOffset
141: 	n.InterfaceHelp = InterfaceHelp
142: 	n.goarch = runtime.GOARCH
143: 
144: 	speeds, err := portSpeeds(n.kindSpecificCfg(), dataNICLimit(n.goarch)+1)
145: 	if err != nil {
146: 		return err
147: 	}
148: 	n.Cfg.Env[portSpeedsEnv] = speeds
149: 
150: 	return nil
151: }
152: 
153: // kindSpecificCfg returns the node's kind-specific config (port-speeds).
154: func (n *mikrotikCHR) kindSpecificCfg() *KindSpecificConfig {
155: 	return kindSpecificConfig.Of(n.Cfg)
156: }
157: 
158: // dataNICLimit is the highest data NIC index the launcher's NIC layout holds on goarch.
159: func dataNICLimit(goarch string) int {
160: 	if goarch == "arm64" {
161: 		return maxDataNICIndexARM64
162: 	}
163: 
164: 	return maxDataNICIndex
165: }
166: 
167: // CheckInterfaceName rejects data NIC indices the launcher does not create: beyond the
168: // tested PCI-bridge layout on amd64, or the free PCI slots on arm64.
169: func (n *mikrotikCHR) CheckInterfaceName() error {
170: 	if err := n.VRNode.CheckInterfaceName(); err != nil {
171: 		return err
172: 	}
173: 
174: 	limit := dataNICLimit(n.goarch)
175: 	for _, ep := range n.Endpoints {
176: 		ifName := ep.GetIfaceName()
177: 		// Name the interface as written in the topology (etherN), with its ethN mapping.
178: 		shown := fmt.Sprintf("%q", ep.GetIfaceDisplayName())
179: 		if ep.GetIfaceDisplayName() != ifName {
180: 			shown += " (" + ifName + ")"
181: 		}
182: 		index, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(ifName, "eth"))
183: 		// An index too large for an int is still an index over the limit.
184: 		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, strconv.ErrRange) {
185: 			return fmt.Errorf(
186: 				"node %q interface %s: cannot parse interface index: %w",
187: 				n.Cfg.ShortName, shown, err,
188: 			)
189: 		}
190: 		if err != nil || index > limit {
191: 			return fmt.Errorf(
192: 				"node %q interface %s exceeds the maximum data NIC index %d on %s (eth%d / ether%d)",
193: 				n.Cfg.ShortName,
194: 				shown,
195: 				limit,
196: 				n.goarch,
197: 				limit,
198: 				limit+1,
199: 			)
200: 		}
201: 	}
202: 
203: 	return nil
204: }
205: 
206: // startPeriod is the healthcheck start period in seconds: the launcher's own worst case
207: // before the ready file, so a slow boot (TCG) never reports unhealthy. It waits up to
208: // CHR_INTF_WAIT for the links, then up to CHR_BOOT_WAIT each for REST, the VRF
209: // handoff, the startup-config import and the SSH banner, plus fetch and gateway checks
210: // and re-plugging NICs RouterOS rejected.
211: func startPeriod(env map[string]string) int {
212: 	return envSeconds(env, "CHR_INTF_WAIT", defaultIntfWait) +
213: 		4*envSeconds(env, "CHR_BOOT_WAIT", defaultBootWait) + startPeriodSlack + replugWait
214: }
215: 
216: // envSeconds reads a positive number of seconds from env, else returns def (the launcher
217: // falls back to its default the same way).
218: func envSeconds(env map[string]string, key string, def int) int {
219: 	if v, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(env[key])); err == nil && v > 0 {
220: 		return v
221: 	}
222: 
223: 	return def
224: }
225: 
226: // PreDeploy writes the launcher next to the startup config on every deploy, so a
227: // containerlab upgrade ships its launcher to existing labs.
228: func (n *mikrotikCHR) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {
229: 	if err := n.VRNode.PreDeploy(ctx, params); err != nil {
230: 		return err
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	dst := filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName)
234: 	if err := os.WriteFile(dst, launcherScript, clabconstants.PermissionsFileDefault); err != nil {
235: 		return fmt.Errorf("node %q: failed to write %s: %w", n.Cfg.ShortName, dst, err)
236: 	}
237: 
238: 	return nil
239: }
240: 
241: // PreStop skips VRNode's vrnetlab qcow2 alias step, which does not apply to this image.
242: func (*mikrotikCHR) PreStop(_ context.Context) error {
243: 	return nil
244: }
245: 
246: // SaveConfig exports the RouterOS configuration over SSH (scrapligo has no RouterOS
247: // platform, see clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH) and writes it as the node's startup config,
248: // without the objects the launcher creates at every boot. Explicit discovery=static
249: // and vrf=main settings retain user choices that compact export omits as defaults,
250: // without adding unrelated verbose defaults that older RouterOS may not understand.
251: func (n *mikrotikCHR) SaveConfig(ctx context.Context) (*clabnodes.SaveConfigResult, error) {
252: 	exported, err := clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH(
253: 		net.JoinHostPort(n.Cfg.LongName, "22"),
254: 		n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
255: 		n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
256: 		`/export; :if ([/ip neighbor discovery-settings get discover-interface-list] = "static") `+
257: 			`do={:put "/ip neighbor discovery-settings set discover-interface-list=static"}; `+
258: 			`:foreach s in=[/ip service find where dynamic=no vrf=main] do={`+
259: 			`:put ("/ip service set [find where name=" . [/ip service get $s name] . " dynamic=no] vrf=main")}; `+
260: 			`:if ([/snmp get vrf] = "main") do={:put "/snmp set vrf=main"}`,
261: 	)
262: 	if err != nil {
263: 		return nil, err
264: 	}
265: 
266: 	return clabnodes.WriteSavedConfig(ctx, n.Cfg, n.ConfigDirName, n.StartupCfgFName,
267: 		[]byte(filterLauncherConfig(exported)+"\n"))
268: }
269: 
270: // filterLauncherConfig drops what the launcher configures at every boot from an /export:
271: // every object tagged clab-mgmt (the ether1 management addresses, the mgmt VRF,
272: // its default routes and the discovery lists), the ether1 ND entry and CHR's ether1
273: // DHCP client. Imported again as a startup config, these lines duplicate objects the
274: // launcher already created and RouterOS stops the import at the first one; management addressing
275: // belongs to
276: // the deployment, not the lab. Continuation lines (an unescaped trailing backslash) are joined
277: // before matching.
278: func filterLauncherConfig(config string) string {
279: 	var out []string
280: 
281: 	section := ""
282: 	pending := ""
283: 	keymatHeader := ""
284: 	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.ReplaceAll(config, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n") {
285: 		if pending != "" {
286: 			line = pending + "\n" + line
287: 			pending = ""
288: 		}
289: 		if continues(line) {
290: 			pending = line
291: 			continue
292: 		}
293: 
294: 		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
295: 		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "/") {
296: 			section = trimmed
297: 			keymatHeader = ""
298: 			// Older RouterOS releases reject even an empty keymat menu. Emit
299: 			// its header only if a command remains after filtering below.
300: 			if section == "/system keymat-provider" {
301: 				keymatHeader = line
302: 				continue
303: 			}
304: 		}
305: 		if launcherOwned(section, trimmed) {
306: 			continue
307: 		}
308: 		// Repeated RouterOS exports can include this disabled factory QKD
309: 		// placeholder. Fresh imports reject it (duplicate name or empty KME
310: 		// address). Drop only this exact entry; keep configured providers.
311: 		if section == "/system keymat-provider" &&
312: 			strings.Join(strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(trimmed, `\`, "")), " ") ==
313: 				"add disabled=yes key-size=0 name=default qkd-cache-size=0 qkd-certificate=*0 type=qkd" {
314: 			continue
315: 		}
316: 		if keymatHeader != "" && trimmed != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
317: 			out = append(out, keymatHeader)
318: 			keymatHeader = ""
319: 		}
320: 		out = append(out, line)
321: 	}
322: 	if pending != "" {
323: 		if keymatHeader != "" {
324: 			out = append(out, keymatHeader)
325: 		}
326: 		out = append(out, pending)
327: 	}
328: 
329: 	return strings.Join(out, "\n")
330: }
331: 
332: // continues reports whether an /export line continues on the next one: it ends in an
333: // unescaped backslash. RouterOS writes a literal backslash in a value as `\\`, so an even
334: // run of trailing backslashes ends the line.
335: func continues(line string) bool {
336: 	trailing := len(line) - len(strings.TrimRight(line, `\`))
337: 
338: 	return trailing%2 == 1
339: }
340: 
341: func launcherOwned(section, line string) bool {
342: 	if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "add ") {
343: 		return false
344: 	}
345: 
346: 	fields := strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(line, `\`, " "))
347: 	has := func(kv string) bool { return slices.Contains(fields, kv) }
348: 
349: 	if has("comment=" + mgmtComment) {
350: 		return true
351: 	}
352: 
353: 	// /ipv6 nd keeps no comment: the launcher's ether1 entry is matched by interface.
354: 	switch section {
355: 	case "/ip address", "/ipv6 address", "/ip dhcp-client", "/ipv6 nd":
356: 		return has("interface=ether1")
357: 	}
358: 
359: 	return false
360: }

        "text": "// Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs\n// Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n\n// Package mikrotik_chr runs MikroTik RouterOS CHR from the official mikrotik/chr image.\n//\n// The image is MikroTik's own distribution (Alpine + qemu + the CHR disk) and is used\n// unmodified: the kind writes chr-launch.sh into the node's lab directory, bind-mounts it\n// read-only and sets it as the entrypoint in place of the image's /start.sh, which is not\n// orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116, #3464).\npackage mikrotik_chr\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\t_ \"embed\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"net\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"path\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"regexp\"\n\t\"runtime\"\n\t\"slices\"\n\t\"strconv\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\n\tclabconstants \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants\"\n\tclabnodes \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes\"\n\tclabtypes \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types\"\n\tclabutils \"github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils\"\n)\n\nvar (\n\tkindNames          = []string{\"mikrotik_chr\"}\n\tdefaultCredentials = clabnodes.NewCredentials(\"admin\", \"admin\")\n\n\tInterfaceRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`ether(?P<port>\\d+)`)\n\tInterfaceOffset = 2\n\tInterfaceHelp   = \"etherX (where X >= 2) or ethX (where X >= 1)\"\n\n\t//go:embed chr-launch.sh\n\tlauncherScript []byte\n)\n\nconst (\n\tconfigDirName   = \"ftpboot\"\n\tstartupCfgFName = \"config.auto.rsc\"\n\n\tlauncherFName = \"chr-launch.sh\"\n\tlauncherPath  = \"/chr-launch.sh\"\n\n\t// readyFile is written by the launcher once RouterOS accepted the credentials and the\n\t// startup config, and removed at every container start.\n\treadyFile = \"/.chr-launch-ready\"\n\n\t// mgmtComment tags every management object the launcher creates in RouterOS.\n\tmgmtComment = \"clab-mgmt\"\n\n\t// amd64's tested PCI-bridge layout. Beyond it the guest runs out of interrupt\n\t// vectors (about 100 NICs per vCPU) and SeaBIOS out of PCI I/O space (8 bridges).\n\tmaxDataNICIndex = 63\n\t// arm64's virt machine gets no PCI bridges: its single bus holds the disk, the\n\t// management NIC and at most 29 data NICs before QEMU runs out of slots.\n\tmaxDataNICIndexARM64 = 29\n\n\t// the launcher's CHR_INTF_WAIT and CHR_BOOT_WAIT defaults, and the time its config\n\t// fetch and gateway check add, in seconds.\n\tdefaultIntfWait  = 60\n\tdefaultBootWait  = 300\n\tstartPeriodSlack = 90\n\t// the launcher's wait for the interface list to settle and its re-plug rounds, in seconds.\n\treplugWait = 180\n\n\tscrapliPlatformName = \"mikrotik_routeros\" //nolint: misspell\n)\n\n// Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.\nfunc Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {\n\tplatformAttrs := &clabnodes.PlatformAttrs{\n\t\tScrapliPlatformName: scrapliPlatformName,\n\t}\n\n\tnrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(defaultCredentials, nil, platformAttrs).\n\t\tWithKindSpecificConfig(kindSpecificConfig)\n\n\tr.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {\n\t\treturn new(mikrotikCHR)\n\t}, nrea)\n}\n\ntype mikrotikCHR struct {\n\tclabnodes.VRNode\n\t// goarch selects the NIC layout the interface limit is checked against. The\n\t// containerlab binary's architecture matches the image's outside emulated setups.\n\tgoarch string\n}\n\nfunc (n *mikrotikCHR) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {\n\tn.VRNode = *clabnodes.NewVRNode(n, defaultCredentials, scrapliPlatformName)\n\tn.ConfigDirName = configDirName\n\tn.StartupCfgFName = startupCfgFName\n\t// The image's qemu falls back to TCG emulation without /dev/kvm: KVM makes the boot\n\t// fast but is not required.\n\tn.HostRequirements.VirtRequired = false\n\n\tn.Cfg = cfg\n\tfor _, o := range opts {\n\t\to(n)\n\t}\n\n\t// Credentials travel as env, not on the command line, so a password needs no quoting.\n\tdefEnv := map[string]string{\n\t\t\"USERNAME\": n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,\n\t\t\"PASSWORD\": n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,\n\t}\n\tn.Cfg.Env = clabutils.MergeStringMaps(defEnv, n.Cfg.Env)\n\n\tn.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds,\n\t\tfmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, configDirName), \":/ftpboot\"),\n\t\tfmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName), \":\", launcherPath, \":ro\"),\n\t)\n\n\tif n.Cfg.Entrypoint == \"\" {\n\t\tn.Cfg.Entrypoint = \"/bin/sh \" + launcherPath\n\t}\n\tn.Cfg.Cmd = fmt.Sprintf(\"--hostname %s\", n.Cfg.ShortName)\n\n\tif n.Cfg.Healthcheck == nil {\n\t\tn.Cfg.Healthcheck = &clabtypes.HealthcheckConfig{\n\t\t\tTest:        []string{\"CMD-SHELL\", \"test -f \" + readyFile},\n\t\t\tInterval:    5,\n\t\t\tTimeout:     3,\n\t\t\tRetries:     3,\n\t\t\tStartPeriod: startPeriod(n.Cfg.Env),\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tn.InterfaceRegexp = InterfaceRegexp\n\tn.InterfaceOffset = InterfaceOffset\n\tn.InterfaceHelp = InterfaceHelp\n\tn.goarch = runtime.GOARCH\n\n\tspeeds, err := portSpeeds(n.kindSpecificCfg(), dataNICLimit(n.goarch)+1)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tn.Cfg.Env[portSpeedsEnv] = speeds\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// kindSpecificCfg returns the node's kind-specific config (port-speeds).\nfunc (n *mikrotikCHR) kindSpecificCfg() *KindSpecificConfig {\n\treturn kindSpecificConfig.Of(n.Cfg)\n}\n\n// dataNICLimit is the highest data NIC index the launcher's NIC layout holds on goarch.\nfunc dataNICLimit(goarch string) int {\n\tif goarch == \"arm64\" {\n\t\treturn maxDataNICIndexARM64\n\t}\n\n\treturn maxDataNICIndex\n}\n\n// CheckInterfaceName rejects data NIC indices the launcher does not create: beyond the\n// tested PCI-bridge layout on amd64, or the free PCI slots on arm64.\nfunc (n *mikrotikCHR) CheckInterfaceName() error {\n\tif err := n.VRNode.CheckInterfaceName(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tlimit := dataNICLimit(n.goarch)\n\tfor _, ep := range n.Endpoints {\n\t\tifName := ep.GetIfaceName()\n\t\t// Name the interface as written in the topology (etherN), with its ethN mapping.\n\t\tshown := fmt.Sprintf(\"%q\", ep.GetIfaceDisplayName())\n\t\tif ep.GetIfaceDisplayName() != ifName {\n\t\t\tshown += \" (\" + ifName + \")\"\n\t\t}\n\t\tindex, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(ifName, \"eth\"))\n\t\t// An index too large for an int is still an index over the limit.\n\t\tif err != nil && !errors.Is(err, strconv.ErrRange) {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\"node %q interface %s: cannot parse interface index: %w\",\n\t\t\t\tn.Cfg.ShortName, shown, err,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err != nil || index > limit {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\"node %q interface %s exceeds the maximum data NIC index %d on %s (eth%d / ether%d)\",\n\t\t\t\tn.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\t\t\tshown,\n\t\t\t\tlimit,\n\t\t\t\tn.goarch,\n\t\t\t\tlimit,\n\t\t\t\tlimit+1,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// startPeriod is the healthcheck start period in seconds: the launcher's own worst case\n// before the ready file, so a slow boot (TCG) never reports unhealthy. It waits up to\n// CHR_INTF_WAIT for the links, then up to CHR_BOOT_WAIT each for REST, the VRF\n// handoff, the startup-config import and the SSH banner, plus fetch and gateway checks\n// and re-plugging NICs RouterOS rejected.\nfunc startPeriod(env map[string]string) int {\n\treturn envSeconds(env, \"CHR_INTF_WAIT\", defaultIntfWait) +\n\t\t4*envSeconds(env, \"CHR_BOOT_WAIT\", defaultBootWait) + startPeriodSlack + replugWait\n}\n\n// envSeconds reads a positive number of seconds from env, else returns def (the launcher\n// falls back to its default the same way).\nfunc envSeconds(env map[string]string, key string, def int) int {\n\tif v, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(env[key])); err == nil && v > 0 {\n\t\treturn v\n\t}\n\n\treturn def\n}\n\n// PreDeploy writes the launcher next to the startup config on every deploy, so a\n// containerlab upgrade ships its launcher to existing labs.\nfunc (n *mikrotikCHR) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {\n\tif err := n.VRNode.PreDeploy(ctx, params); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tdst := filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName)\n\tif err := os.WriteFile(dst, launcherScript, clabconstants.PermissionsFileDefault); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"node %q: failed to write %s: %w\", n.Cfg.ShortName, dst, err)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// PreStop skips VRNode's vrnetlab qcow2 alias step, which does not apply to this image.\nfunc (*mikrotikCHR) PreStop(_ context.Context) error {\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// SaveConfig exports the RouterOS configuration over SSH (scrapligo has no RouterOS\n// platform, see clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH) and writes it as the node's startup config,\n// without the objects the launcher creates at every boot. Explicit discovery=static\n// and vrf=main settings retain user choices that compact export omits as defaults,\n// without adding unrelated verbose defaults that older RouterOS may not understand.\nfunc (n *mikrotikCHR) SaveConfig(ctx context.Context) (*clabnodes.SaveConfigResult, error) {\n\texported, err := clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH(\n\t\tnet.JoinHostPort(n.Cfg.LongName, \"22\"),\n\t\tn.Cfg.Credentials.Username,\n\t\tn.Cfg.Credentials.Password,\n\t\t`/export; :if ([/ip neighbor discovery-settings get discover-interface-list] = \"static\") `+\n\t\t\t`do={:put \"/ip neighbor discovery-settings set discover-interface-list=static\"}; `+\n\t\t\t`:foreach s in=[/ip service find where dynamic=no vrf=main] do={`+\n\t\t\t`:put (\"/ip service set [find where name=\" . [/ip service get $s name] . \" dynamic=no] vrf=main\")}; `+\n\t\t\t`:if ([/snmp get vrf] = \"main\") do={:put \"/snmp set vrf=main\"}`,\n\t)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\treturn clabnodes.WriteSavedConfig(ctx, n.Cfg, n.ConfigDirName, n.StartupCfgFName,\n\t\t[]byte(filterLauncherConfig(exported)+\"\\n\"))\n}\n\n// filterLauncherConfig drops what the launcher configures at every boot from an /export:\n// every object tagged clab-mgmt (the ether1 management addresses, the mgmt VRF,\n// its default routes and the discovery lists), the ether1 ND entry and CHR's ether1\n// DHCP client. Imported again as a startup config, these lines duplicate objects the\n// launcher already created and RouterOS stops the import at the first one; management addressing\n// belongs to\n// the deployment, not the lab. Continuation lines (an unescaped trailing backslash) are joined\n// before matching.\nfunc filterLauncherConfig(config string) string {\n\tvar out []string\n\n\tsection := \"\"\n\tpending := \"\"\n\tkeymatHeader := \"\"\n\tfor line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.ReplaceAll(config, \"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\"), \"\\n\") {\n\t\tif pending != \"\" {\n\t\t\tline = pending + \"\\n\" + line\n\t\t\tpending = \"\"\n\t\t}\n\t\tif continues(line) {\n\t\t\tpending = line\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\ttrimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)\n\t\tif strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, \"/\") {\n\t\t\tsection = trimmed\n\t\t\tkeymatHeader = \"\"\n\t\t\t// Older RouterOS releases reject even an empty keymat menu. Emit\n\t\t\t// its header only if a command remains after filtering below.\n\t\t\tif section == \"/system keymat-provider\" {\n\t\t\t\tkeymatHeader = line\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif launcherOwned(section, trimmed) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Repeated RouterOS exports can include this disabled factory QKD\n\t\t// placeholder. Fresh imports reject it (duplicate name or empty KME\n\t\t// address). Drop only this exact entry; keep configured providers.\n\t\tif section == \"/system keymat-provider\" &&\n\t\t\tstrings.Join(strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(trimmed, `\\`, \"\")), \" \") ==\n\t\t\t\t\"add disabled=yes key-size=0 name=default qkd-cache-size=0 qkd-certificate=*0 type=qkd\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif keymatHeader != \"\" && trimmed != \"\" && !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, \"#\") {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, keymatHeader)\n\t\t\tkeymatHeader = \"\"\n\t\t}\n\t\tout = append(out, line)\n\t}\n\tif pending != \"\" {\n\t\tif keymatHeader != \"\" {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, keymatHeader)\n\t\t}\n\t\tout = append(out, pending)\n\t}\n\n\treturn strings.Join(out, \"\\n\")\n}\n\n// continues reports whether an /export line continues on the next one: it ends in an\n// unescaped backslash. RouterOS writes a literal backslash in a value as `\\\\`, so an even\n// run of trailing backslashes ends the line.\nfunc continues(line string) bool {\n\ttrailing := len(line) - len(strings.TrimRight(line, `\\`))\n\n\treturn trailing%2 == 1\n}\n\nfunc launcherOwned(section, line string) bool {\n\tif !strings.HasPrefix(line, \"add \") {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\n\tfields := strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(line, `\\`, \" \"))\n\thas := func(kv string) bool { return slices.Contains(fields, kv) }\n\n\tif has(\"comment=\" + mgmtComment) {\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\n\t// /ipv6 nd keeps no comment: the launcher's ether1 entry is matched by interface.\n\tswitch section {\n\tcase \"/ip address\", \"/ipv6 address\", \"/ip dhcp-client\", \"/ipv6 nd\":\n\t\treturn has(\"interface=ether1\")\n\t}\n\n\treturn false\n}",

1: package nodes
2: 
3: import (
4: 	"errors"
5: 	"fmt"
6: 	"regexp"
7: 	"strings"
8: 
9: 	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
10: 	"gopkg.in/yaml.v2"
11: )
12: 
13: // KindSpecificConfigType is a kind's config type, registered with
14: // NodeRegistryEntryAttributes.WithKindSpecificConfig. Only KindSpecificConfigSpec implements it.
15: type KindSpecificConfigType interface {
16: 	newKindSpecificConfig() any
17: }
18: 
19: // KindSpecificConfigSpec binds a kind to its config struct T, which holds the kind-specific keys of
20: // a node
21: // definition. A kind declares one spec, registers it and reads node configs through it:
22: //
23: //	var kindSpecificConfig clabnodes.KindSpecificConfigSpec[KindSpecificConfig]
24: //
25: //	nrea.WithKindSpecificConfig(kindSpecificConfig)
26: //	func (n *iol) kindSpecificCfg() *KindSpecificConfig { return kindSpecificConfig.Of(n.Cfg) }
27: //
28: // T must not implement yaml.Unmarshaler itself; its fields may.
29: type KindSpecificConfigSpec[T any] struct{}
30: 
31: // KindSpecificConfigDefaulter is implemented by kind-specific configs whose defaults are not the
32: // zero value.
33: // Topology keys decode on top of the defaults.
34: type KindSpecificConfigDefaulter interface {
35: 	SetDefaults()
36: }
37: 
38: func (KindSpecificConfigSpec[T]) newKindSpecificConfig() any {
39: 	return newDefaultKindSpecificConfig[T]()
40: }
41: 
42: func newDefaultKindSpecificConfig[T any]() *T {
43: 	t := new(T)
44: 	if d, ok := any(t).(KindSpecificConfigDefaulter); ok {
45: 		d.SetDefaults()
46: 	}
47: 
48: 	return t
49: }
50: 
51: // Of returns cfg's kind-specific config, setting a default T when cfg has none (e.g. a node config
52: // built
53: // outside the topology). A kind-specific config of another type is a programming error and panics.
54: func (KindSpecificConfigSpec[T]) Of(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig) *T {
55: 	switch kc := cfg.KindSpecificConfig.(type) {
56: 	case *T:
57: 		return kc
58: 	case nil:
59: 		t := newDefaultKindSpecificConfig[T]()
60: 		cfg.KindSpecificConfig = t
61: 
62: 		return t
63: 	default:
64: 		panic(
65: 			fmt.Sprintf(
66: 				"node %q: kind-specific config is %T, want %T",
67: 				cfg.ShortName,
68: 				kc,
69: 				(*T)(nil),
70: 			),
71: 		)
72: 	}
73: }
74: 
75: // InvalidKindSpecificConfig stands in for a kind-specific config that failed to decode, e.g. from a
76: // state file written before a key changed. ComputeDiff never considers it equal to another
77: // kind-specific config.
78: type InvalidKindSpecificConfig struct {
79: 	Err string
80: }
81: 
82: // acceptsKey reports whether t has key. Strict decoding of `key: null` fails only for unknown
83: // fields, since yaml.v2 does not call field unmarshalers for null.
84: func acceptsKey(t KindSpecificConfigType, key string) bool {
85: 	b, err := yaml.Marshal(map[string]any{key: nil})
86: 	if err != nil {
87: 		return false
88: 	}
89: 
90: 	return yaml.UnmarshalStrict(b, t.newKindSpecificConfig()) == nil
91: }
92: 
93: var yamlLinePrefix = regexp.MustCompile(`^line \d+: `)
94: 
95: // yamlErrorText returns a yaml.v2 error without its line prefixes, which refer to the
96: // re-marshalled key rather than to the topology file.
97: func yamlErrorText(err error) string {
98: 	var typeErr *yaml.TypeError
99: 	if !errors.As(err, &typeErr) {
100: 		return err.Error()
101: 	}
102: 
103: 	msgs := make([]string, 0, len(typeErr.Errors))
104: 	for _, e := range typeErr.Errors {
105: 		msgs = append(msgs, yamlLinePrefix.ReplaceAllString(e, ""))
106: 	}
107: 
108: 	return strings.Join(msgs, "; ")
109: }
110: 
111: // DecodeKindSpecificConfig strictly decodes a node's raw kind-specific config entries into a new
112: // config of the
113: // kind registered in e. It returns a pointer to the kind's config type, or nil for kinds without
114: // a kind-specific config. Every unsupported key and invalid value is reported, naming the block it
115: // was set
116: // in.
117: func DecodeKindSpecificConfig(
118: 	e *NodeRegistryEntry,
119: 	node, kind string,
120: 	entries []clabtypes.KindSpecificConfigEntry,
121: ) (any, error) {
122: 	t := e.KindSpecificConfigType()
123: 
124: 	var kindSpecificConfig any
125: 	if t != nil {
126: 		kindSpecificConfig = t.newKindSpecificConfig()
127: 	}
128: 
129: 	var errs []error
130: 
131: 	for _, en := range entries {
132: 		if t == nil || !acceptsKey(t, en.Key) {
133: 			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("node %q: kind %q does not support key %q (set in %s)",
134: 				node, kind, en.Key, en.From))
135: 
136: 			continue
137: 		}
138: 
139: 		b, err := yaml.Marshal(map[string]any{en.Key: en.Value})
140: 		if err == nil {
141: 			err = yaml.UnmarshalStrict(b, kindSpecificConfig)
142: 		}
143: 
144: 		if err != nil {
145: 			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("node %q: invalid value for key %q (set in %s): %s",
146: 				node, en.Key, en.From, yamlErrorText(err)))
147: 		}
148: 	}
149: 
150: 	if len(errs) > 0 {
151: 		return nil, errors.Join(errs...)
152: 	}
153: 
154: 	return kindSpecificConfig, nil
155: }

(End of file - total 155 lines)

14: // decodeKindSpecificConfig decodes the node's raw kind-specific config keys from topo into its
15: // kind's config type.
16: func (c *CLab) decodeKindSpecificConfig(
17: 	topo *clabtypes.Topology,
18: 	nodeName, kind string,
19: ) (any, error) {
20: 	var entry *clabnodes.NodeRegistryEntry
21: 	if c.Reg != nil {
22: 		entry = c.Reg.Kind(kind)
23: 	}
24: 
25: 	return clabnodes.DecodeKindSpecificConfig(
26: 		entry,
27: 		nodeName,
28: 		kind,
29: 		c.expandKindSpecificConfigMagicVars(
30: 			topo.GetNodeKindSpecificConfig(nodeName),
31: 			nodeName,
32: 		),
33: 	)
34: }
35: 
36: // expandKindSpecificConfigMagicVars replaces magic variables in every string of the given raw
37: // kind-specific config entries. Values are copied, so the topology definitions the entries point
38: // at are left untouched and keep serving other nodes unchanged.
39: func (c *CLab) expandKindSpecificConfigMagicVars(
40: 	entries []clabtypes.KindSpecificConfigEntry,
41: 	nodeName string,
42: ) []clabtypes.KindSpecificConfigEntry {
43: 	if c.TopoPaths == nil || !c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileIsSet() {
44: 		// Without the topology paths the magic variables cannot be resolved; the entries are
45: 		// returned as parsed.
46: 		return entries
47: 	}
48: 
49: 	r := c.magicVarReplacer(nodeName)
50: 
51: 	var expand func(any) any
52: 
53: 	expand = func(v any) any {
54: 		switch v := v.(type) {
55: 		case string:
56: 			return r.Replace(v)
57: 		case []any:
58: 			out := make([]any, len(v))
59: 			for i, e := range v {
60: 				out[i] = expand(e)
61: 			}
62: 
63: 			return out
64: 		case map[string]any:
65: 			out := make(map[string]any, len(v))
66: 			for k, e := range v {
67: 				out[k] = expand(e)
68: 			}
69: 
70: 			return out
71: 		case map[any]any:
72: 			out := make(map[any]any, len(v))
73: 			for k, e := range v {
74: 				out[expand(k)] = expand(e)
75: 			}
76: 
77: 			return out
78: 		default:
79: 			return v
80: 		}
81: 	}
82: 
83: 	out := make([]clabtypes.KindSpecificConfigEntry, len(entries))
84: 	for i, e := range entries {
85: 		out[i] = e
86: 		out[i].Value = expand(e.Value)
87: 	}
88: 
89: 	return out
90: }

92: // validateKindSpecificConfigKeys checks the kind-specific config keys of the defaults, kinds and
93: // groups blocks,
94: // including blocks no node uses: keys under kinds.<kind> must belong to that kind, keys of a
95: // defaults or group block that sets a kind must belong to that kind, and every other key must
96: // belong to at least one kind. Node blocks are checked when each node's kind-specific config is
97: // decoded.
98: func (c *CLab) validateKindSpecificConfigKeys() error {
99: 	if c.Reg == nil {
100: 		return nil
101: 	}
102: 
103: 	topo := c.Config.Topology
104: 
105: 	var errs []error
106: 
107: 	check := func(from, kind string, def *clabtypes.NodeDefinition) {
108: 		if def == nil {
109: 			return
110: 		}
111: 
112: 		for _, key := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(def.KindSpecificConfig)) {
113: 			switch {
114: 			case kind != "":
115: 				if !c.Reg.Kind(kind).AcceptsKindSpecificConfigKey(key) {
116: 					errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("kind %q does not support key %q (set in %s)",
117: 						kind, key, from))
118: 				}
119: 			case !c.anyKindAcceptsKindSpecificConfigKey(key):
120: 				errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("no kind supports key %q (set in %s)", key, from))
121: 			}
122: 		}
123: 	}
124: 
125: 	check("defaults", strings.ToLower(topo.GetDefaults().Kind), topo.GetDefaults())
126: 
127: 	for _, name := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(topo.Kinds)) {
128: 		check("kinds."+name, strings.ToLower(name), topo.Kinds[name])
129: 	}
130: 
131: 	for _, name := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(topo.Groups)) {
132: 		if def := topo.Groups[name]; def != nil {
133: 			check("groups."+name, strings.ToLower(def.Kind), def)
134: 		}
135: 	}
136: 
137: 	return errors.Join(errs...)
138: }
139: 
140: func (c *CLab) anyKindAcceptsKindSpecificConfigKey(key string) bool {
141: 	for _, kind := range c.Reg.GetRegisteredNodeKindNames() {
142: 		if c.Reg.Kind(kind).AcceptsKindSpecificConfigKey(key) {
143: 			return true
144: 		}
145: 	}
146: 
147: 	return false

Reasoning
Good — the framework handles node>group>kind>defaults precedence with the whole value from the first block. So "node's own port-speeds replaces the group's list" is automatic. The test verifies it.

Now check `AcceptsKindSpecificConfigKey` and the `kindSpecificConfig` var being a zero-size struct value — `WithKindSpecificConfig(kindSpecificConfig)` — fine.

Now important: `kindSpecificConfig.Of(n.Cfg)` in `Init` — panics if `n.Cfg.KindSpecificConfig` is of another type. When could Init be called with a mismatched KindSpecificConfig? Init is called per kind by the registry, so the config was decoded for that kind. But — inspect state-file paths: "InvalidKindSpecificConfig stands in for a kind-specific config that failed to decode, e.g. from a state file written before a key changed." Where does a node get Init'd with a KindSpecificConfig from a state file? E.g. `clab redploy`/`tools sshx`? If `Cfg.KindSpecificConfig` is `*InvalidKindSpecificConfig`, `Of` would panic (type mismatch → default branch → panic). But that's the framework's designed behavior — same as sros/iol etc. Not this PR's issue. Wait — but before this PR, mikrotik_chr had no kind-specific config; existing saved state files (from before) would have KindSpecificConfig nil → Of sets default → fine.

Hmm — one real concern: state file compatibility. When a lab deployed with an older containerlab (no port-speeds) is redeployed with a new one, ComputeDiff compares kind-specific configs. Before this change, the state was written with KindSpecificConfig nil? Now the new Init always sets CHR_PORT_SPEEDS env, which goes into node config Env — for diff computation, does Env change trigger redeploy? For VR nodes the Env is part of node config. An old state with no CHR_PORT_SPEEDS vs new state with "" (empty)... An empty env var would now appear in every deploy's state. Would ComputeDiff consider Env differences? If yes, every existing mikrotik_chr lab gets redeployed once on upgrade. That's expected for a feature change; not a defect.

Actually wait — setting `n.Cfg.Env[portSpeedsEnv] = speeds` even when speeds is "" means the env var `CHR_PORT_SPEEDS=` (empty) is always set on the container. The launcher handles empty via `${CHR_PORT_SPEEDS:-}`. Fine.

Now the launcher. Let me read the relevant sections of chr-launch.sh head: around data_nic_speed, bridge_eth, and check `set -e` / shellcheck disables, and how `log` works. Also check the re-plug path uses data_nic_device (so speed is included — test says so).

1: #!/bin/sh
2: # chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud
3: # Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.
4: #
5: # The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +
6: # /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the
7: # node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces
8: # the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):
9: # it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the
10: # management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no
11: # startup config.
12: #
13: # What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done
14: # with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):
15: #   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)
16: #   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's
17: #      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS
18: #      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: management services
19: #      reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only
20: #      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred
21: #   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,
22: #      LLDP and LACP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so
23: #      container ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps
24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is
25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,
26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return
27: #      path in its own VRF (`mgmt`, below), then fetches
28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)
29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it
30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu
31: #
32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an
33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW
34: # device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never
35: # binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is
36: # recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are
37: # persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu
38: # carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and
39: # their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management
40: # step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.
41: #
42: # Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,
43: #   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.
44: # Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]
45: #   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env
46: # Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the
47: #   official image's own variables:
48: #   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),
49: #   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)
50: # Serial console: port 5000 inside the container
51: #   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no
52: #   address on the management network.
53: # Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default
54: #   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.
55: # Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed "chr-launch:":
56: #   "RouterOS ready"                   login + startup config done
57: #   "startup config import FAILED: …"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's
58: #                                      own reason, with the line number)
59: #   "credential bootstrap FAILED: …"   the user/password step failed
60: #   "management setup FAILED: …"       the ether1 address / mgmt VRF step failed
61: #   "data NIC check FAILED: …"         RouterOS lacks an interface for a data NIC
62: #                                      even after re-plugging it (also checked
63: #                                      after a reboot from inside RouterOS)
64: #   "RouterOS did not answer within …  after a reboot from inside RouterOS; the
65: #    after the reboot: not ready"      launcher keeps waiting and checks later
66: #
67: # Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs
68: # Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
69: # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
70: 
71: set -u
72: 
73: # Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting
74: # limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.
75: USERNAME="${USERNAME:-admin}"
76: PASSWORD="${PASSWORD-admin}"
77: HOSTNAME_ARG=""
78: while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
79:     case "$1" in
80:         --username) USERNAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
81:         --password) PASSWORD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
82:         --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
83:         --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;
84:         --trace) shift ;;
85:         *) shift ;;
86:     esac
87: done
88: [ -n "$HOSTNAME_ARG" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG="$(hostname)"
89: 
90: CPUS="${CPUS:-1}"
91: DISK="${DISK:-128M}"
92: INTF_WAIT="${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}"
93: BOOT_WAIT="${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}"
94: INTFS="${CLAB_INTFS:-0}"
95: STARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc
96: # Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the
97: # container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).
98: DONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped
99: READY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready
100: ID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id
101: NICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics
102: MGMT_TABLE=mgmt
103: # every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each
104: # boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out
105: MGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt
106: MGMT_BR=br0
107: # eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network
108: # namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare
109: MGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt
110: SYSNET=/sys/class/net
111: 
112: log() { echo "chr-launch: $*"; }
113: rm -f "$READY_FILE"
114: 
115: FETCH_PORT=8080
116: # QEMU's QMP monitors, inside the container only: one re-plugs NICs RouterOS
117: # rejected at boot, the other reports guest reboots
118: QMP_PORT=5001
119: QMP_EVENT_PORT=5002
120: 
121: # ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------
122: IMG=""
123: for f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f "$f" ] && IMG="$f" && break; done
124: if [ -z "$IMG" ]; then
125:     log "no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image"
126:     exit 1
127: fi
128: # Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.
129: disk_bytes() {
130:     case "$1" in
131:         *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
132:         *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
133:         *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;
134:         *) echo "$1" ;;
135:     esac
136: }
137: want_bytes="$(disk_bytes "$DISK")"
138: cur_bytes="$(stat -c %s "$IMG" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < "$IMG")"
139: if [ "$cur_bytes" -lt "$want_bytes" ] 2>/dev/null; then
140:     truncate -s "$DISK" "$IMG"

The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management\n# step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.\n#\n# Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,\n#   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.\n# Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]\n#   (unknown flags are ignored);
