196: 
197: check_nic_index() { # check_nic_index <max-index>: reject indices beyond the NIC layout
198:     # 63 NICs behind bridges are tested. More run into the guest's interrupt
199:     # vectors (about 100 NICs per vCPU) and SeaBIOS's PCI I/O space (8 bridges).
200:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" = 1 ] && [ "$1" -gt 63 ]; then
201:         log "at most 63 data NICs are supported (eth63 / ether64); index $1 is beyond the tested limit"
202:         return 1
203:     fi
204:     # Without bridges (arm64 virt) one bus holds the disk, management and 29 data NICs.
205:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" != 1 ] && [ "$1" -gt 29 ]; then
206:         log "at most 29 data NICs fit without PCI bridges (eth29 / ether30); index $1 leaves no PCI slot for the disk"
207:         return 1
208:     fi
209: }
210: 
211: data_nic_speed() { # data_nic_speed <index>: the data NIC's speed in Mb/s
212:     # The kind writes the validated port-speeds key to CHR_PORT_SPEEDS as
213:     # "<port>:<Mb/s>" pairs; data NIC <index> is ether<index+1>. Other ports
214:     # report 10G, the speed a container veth reports.
215:     for _pair in ${CHR_PORT_SPEEDS:-}; do
216:         [ "${_pair%%:*}" = "$(( $1 + 1 ))" ] && { printf '%s' "${_pair#*:}"; return; }
217:     done
218:     printf '%s' 10000
219: }
220: 
221: data_nic_device() { # data_nic_device <index> <mac>: the NIC's -device value (also used to re-plug it)
222:     # A virtio NIC reports no speed and half duplex unless told otherwise, and
223:     # RouterOS bonds in 802.3ad mode only with full-duplex ports.
224:     _link="speed=$(data_nic_speed "$1"),duplex=full"
225:     case "$PCI_BRIDGES" in
226:         1)
227:             # The default PC has only 29 free PCI slots, including management.
228:             # Keep management on the root bus and put data NICs behind bridges.
229:             # Follow vrnetlab's conservative allocation of 25 NICs per bridge.
230:             # Omit PXE ROMs to avoid exhausting SeaBIOS option-ROM space.
231:             # Keep MSI-X, but share one vector between RX/TX queues (plus one
232:             # for config) to reduce IRQ pressure.
233:             # Disabling MSI-X entirely can leave NICs missing in RouterOS.
234:             printf '%s' "virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2,bus=chrpci$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 )),addr=$(printf '0x%x' $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 + 1 ))),romfile=,vectors=2,$_link"
235:             ;;
236:         *)
237:             # ARM64 uses the virt machine and keeps its existing NIC layout.
238:             printf '%s' "virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2,$_link"
239:             ;;
240:     esac
241: }
242: 
243: qemu_data_nic() { # qemu_data_nic <index> <mac>: append-only QEMU arguments
244:     # Each bridge comes right before its first NIC.
245:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" = 1 ] && [ $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 )) -eq 0 ]; then
246:         _bridge=$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 ))
247:         printf '%s ' "-device pci-bridge,id=chrpci$_bridge,chassis_nr=$_bridge,bus=pci.0"
248:     fi
249:     printf '%s' "-netdev tap,id=d$1,ifname=tap$1,script=no,downscript=no -device $(data_nic_device "$1" "$2")"
250: }
251: 
252: # ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----
253: ip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix
254:     ip -"$1" addr show dev "$2" 2>/dev/null \
255:         | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\{0,1\} \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
256: }
257: ip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway
258:     ip -"$1" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
259: }
260: M4="$(ip_global 4 eth0)"; M6="$(ip_global 6 eth0)"
261: G4="$(ip_gw 4)"; G6="$(ip_gw 6)"
262: if [ -n "$M4$M6" ]; then
263:     printf 'M4=%s\nM6=%s\nG4=%s\nG6=%s\n' "$M4" "$M6" "$G4" "$G6" > "$MGMT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
264: elif [ -f "$MGMT_FILE" ]; then
265:     # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments
266:     . "$MGMT_FILE"
267: fi
268: log "management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}"
269: 
270: tunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap
271: if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR" ]; then
272:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
273:     ip addr flush dev eth0
274:     # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the
275:     # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.
276:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null
277:     brctl addbr "$MGMT_BR"
278:     brctl setfd "$MGMT_BR" 0 2>/dev/null
279:     echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
280:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" address "52:54:01:$node_id:00"
281:     ip link set tap0 mtu "$_mtu"
282:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" mtu "$_mtu"
283:     # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until
284:     # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's
285:     # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.
286:     brctl addif "$MGMT_BR" tap0
287:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \
288:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0" "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0" \
289:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0" 2>/dev/null
290: fi
291: ip link set tap0 up
292: ip link set "$MGMT_BR" up
293: # RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it
294: VM_LL="fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00"
295: VM_EP="$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR"
296: # The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read
297: # once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and
298: # the address stays tentative.
299: LL=""
300: bridge_ll() {
301:     _w=0
302:     while [ -z "$LL" ] && [ "$_w" -lt 20 ]; do
303:         LL="$(ip -6 addr show dev "$MGMT_BR" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \
304:             | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \(fe80::[^/]*\)\/64 .*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
305:         [ -n "$LL" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }
306:     done
307:     [ -n "$LL" ] || log "no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR"
308: }
309: 
310: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk
311: # eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS
312: # numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count
313: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and
314: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the
315: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes
316: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.
317: max=0
318: for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
319:     [ -e "$d" ] || continue
320:     n="${d##*/eth}"
321:     [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] && max="$n"
322: done
323: prev="$(cat "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
324: case "$prev" in *[!0-9]*|"") prev=0 ;; esac
325: [ "$prev" -gt "$max" ] && max="$prev"
326: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after
327: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and
328: # the watcher bridges the late veths.
329: case "$INTFS" in *[!0-9]*|"") INTFS=0 ;; esac
330: [ "$INTFS" -gt "$max" ] && max="$INTFS"
331: check_nic_index "$max" || exit 1
332: [ "$max" -gt "$prev" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$max" > "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true; }
333: 
334: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system
335: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse
336: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.
337: if [ -z "${MEM:-}" ]; then
338:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))
339: fi
340: 
341: bridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)
342:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
343:     if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$1" ]; then
344:         brctl addbr "br$1"
345:         ip link set "br$1" mtu "$_mtu"
346:         ip link set "tap$1" mtu "$_mtu"
347:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14). The bridge refuses LACP
348:         # (01:80:c2:00:00:02, bit 2), so each port forwards it (below).
349:         echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
350:         brctl addif "br$1" "tap$1"
351:         echo 4 > "$SYSNET/tap$1/brport/group_fwd_mask" ||
352:             log "could not enable LACP forwarding on tap$1 (bridge br$1)"
353:     fi
354:     brctl addif "br$1" "eth$1"

The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes\n# back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.\nmax=0\nfor d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n    [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n    n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n    [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$n\"\ndone\nprev=\"$(cat \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\ncase \"$prev\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") prev=0 ;; esac\n[ \"$prev\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$prev\"\n# The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after\n# every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and\n# the watcher bridges the late veths.\ncase \"$INTFS\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") INTFS=0 ;; esac\n[ \"$INTFS\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$INTFS\"\ncheck_nic_index \"$max\" || exit 1\n[ \"$max\" -gt \"$prev\" ] && { printf '%s\\n' \"$max\" > \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true; }\n\n# RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system\n# requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse\n# link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.\nif [ -z \"${MEM:-}\" ]; then\n    MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))\nfi\n\nbridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)\n    _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n    if [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$1\" ]; then\n        brctl addbr \"br$1\"\n        ip link set \"br$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n        ip link set \"tap$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n        # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14). The bridge refuses LACP\n        # (01:80:c2:00:00:02, bit 2), so each port forwards it (below).\n        echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n        brctl addif \"br$1\" \"tap$1\"\n        echo 4 > \"$SYSNET/tap$1/brport/group_fwd_mask\" ||\n            log \"could not enable LACP forwarding on tap$1 (bridge br$1)\"\n    fi\n    brctl addif \"br$1\" \"eth$1\"",

355:     echo 4 > "$SYSNET/eth$1/brport/group_fwd_mask" ||
356:         log "could not enable LACP forwarding on eth$1 (bridge br$1)"
357:     ip link set "eth$1" up

359: }
360: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link
361: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's
362: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS
363: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.
364: watch_links() {
365:     _warned=""
366:     while kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
367:         i=1
368:         while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
369:             if [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i" ]; then
370:                 bridge_eth "$i" && log "link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i"
371:             fi
372:             i=$((i + 1))
373:         done
374:         for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
375:             [ -e "$d" ] || continue
376:             n="${d##*/eth}"
377:             [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] || continue
378:             case " $_warned " in *" $n "*) continue ;; esac
379:             _warned="$_warned $n"
380:             log "link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted"
381:         done
382:         sleep 2
383:     done
384: }
385: 
386: i=1
387: speeds=""
388: while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
389:     tap="tap$i"
390:     tunctl -t "$tap" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev "$tap" mode tap
391:     [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && bridge_eth "$i"
392:     ip link set "$tap" up
393:     NET="$NET $(qemu_data_nic "$i" "$(nic_mac "$i")")"
394:     speeds="$speeds ether$((i + 1))=$(data_nic_speed "$i")"
395:     i=$((i + 1))
396: done
397: # One line with the speed of every data NIC, so a port-speeds entry for a
398: # port this node does not create is visible here.
399: [ "$max" -gt 0 ] && log "data NIC speeds (Mb/s):$speeds"
400: 
401: # shellcheck disable=SC2086
402: $QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \
403:     -qmp "tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_PORT,server,nowait" \
404:     -qmp "tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_EVENT_PORT,server,nowait" \
405:     -m "$MEM" -smp "cpus=$CPUS" \
406:     -drive "file=$IMG,format=raw" \
407:     -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \
408:     $NET &
409: QEMU_PID=$!
410: trap 'kill "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT
411: log "qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)"
412: watch_links &

414: # ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
415: json_str() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g'; }
416: rest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]
417:     # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI
418:     # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the
419:     # read timeout (default 20s).
420:     _auth="Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')"
421:     if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then
422:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
423:             --header "$_auth" --post-data "$3" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
424:     else
425:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "$_auth" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
426:     fi
427: }
428: # busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts
429: # its diagnosis ONLY there ({"detail":"Script Error: … (line N column M)"}; its
430: # /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw
431: # HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,
432: # reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite
433: # `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed
434: # once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.
435: resp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived
436:     _cl="$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')"
437:     [ -n "$_cl" ] || return 1
438:     grep -q -m1 '^\r*$' "$1" 2>/dev/null || return 1
439:     [ "$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$1" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" -ge "$_cl" ]
440: }
441: rest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> "<status> <body>"
442:     _f="/tmp/chr-rest.$$"; rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"; mkfifo "$_f" || return 1
443:     timeout "$(( $4 + 5 ))" nc "$VM_EP" 80 <"$_f" >"$_f.out" 2>/dev/null &
444:     _pid=$!
445:     exec 7>"$_f"
446:     printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: [%s]\r\nAuthorization: Basic %s\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n%s' \
447:         "$2" "$VM_LL" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" \
448:         "$(printf '%s' "$3" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" "$3" >&7
449:     _left=$4
450:     while kill -0 "$_pid" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete "$_f.out" && [ "$_left" -gt 0 ]; do
451:         sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))
452:     done
453:     exec 7>&-
454:     wait "$_pid" 2>/dev/null
455:     _st="$(head -n1 "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)"
456:     _body="$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')"
457:     rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"
458:     printf '%s %s' "${_st:-000}" "$_body"
459: }
460: # RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a
461: # bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently
462: # failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.
463: is_err() { case "$1" in *'"error"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }
464: 
465: # ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------
466: waited=0
467: AUTH=""
468: # A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank
469: # password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username
470: # asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that
471: # answers is the requested user.
472: while [ -z "$AUTH" ]; do
473:     for _cred in "admin:" "admin:$PASSWORD" "$USERNAME:$PASSWORD"; do
474:         rest "$_cred" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH="$_cred"; break; }

Reasoning
Now, the bridge_eth LACP forwarding detail. Wait — there's a subtle issue: `echo 4 > "$SYSNET/tap$1/brport/group_fwd_mask"` happens inside the `if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$1" ]` block, right after `brctl addif "br$1" "tap$1"` — good, tap$1 has a brport dir at that point. And `echo 4 > eth$1/brport/group_fwd_mask` happens after `brctl addif br$1 eth$1`. Both fine.

However — the per-port `group_fwd_mask` semantics: In the kernel, the per-port group_fwd_mask is OR'd with... hmm. Actually in the kernel, per-port group_fwd_mask can only *add* forwarding for frames the bridge-level mask would drop? The check is `(br->group_fwd_mask & mask) || (p->group_fwd_mask & mask)` — OR'd. But wait — is there any restriction? I recall the per-port sysfs file description: "Set the forwarding policy for certain reserved IEEE 802 frames ... on this port. Setting a bit here overrides the bridge's group_fwd_mask." OK. But also — do the bits matter where the frame is *received*? The mask check uses the port the frame arrived on. Frame arriving on tap → forwarded to eth; uses tap's mask. Frame from eth → tap; uses eth's mask. Both set. Good.

One concern: per-port group_fwd_mask was added in kernel 5.??. Actually per-port group_fwd_mask exists since... I believe it's supported in sysfs `br_sysfs_if.c` for a while (5.x). The launcher handles failure with a log. Fine.

Now, a real potential issue: `group_fwd_mask` bit 2 = 01:80:c2:00:00:02 (slow protocols / LACP). Actually the mapping: group_fwd_mask bit N corresponds to address 01:80:c2:00:00:0N? LLDP is 01:80:c2:00:00:0E = bit 14 → 16384. LACP is 01:80:c2:00:00:02 → bit 2 → 4. Correct.

But wait — LACP frames are typically sent to 01:80:c2:00:00:02 which is in the 01:80:c2:00:00:0X reserved range. However, Linux bridges drop these as link-local. There's a subtlety: is link-local processing done before or after the port mask? In br_handle_frame: for link-local addresses, if (br->group_fwd_mask | p->group_fwd_mask) & mask → forward. There is a restricted mask: 01:80:c2:00:00:01 (bit 1)? `#define BR_GROUPFWD_RESTRICTED ...`? I don't recall restrictions on bit 2. Actually I do remember: "The bridge will not forward ... 01:80:c2:00:00:01 (MAC Control, e.g. PAUSE)" regardless. Bit 2 (LACP) is forwardable. Fine.

Now, the `data_nic_speed` function and word splitting. `for _pair in ${CHR_PORT_SPEEDS:-}` — under `set -u`, `${CHR_PORT_SPEEDS:-}` handles unset. Values come from the kind (validated, space-separated, no glob chars). But: the user could set `env: CHR_PORT_SPEEDS: ...` manually with arbitrary content — the kind always overwrites via `n.Cfg.Env[portSpeedsEnv] = speeds` (test "replaces-env" verifies). So only validated content. But wait — could the user set CHR_PORT_SPEEDS in the topology `env:` and have it bypass? Init always overwrites. Order: `n.Cfg.Env = MergeStringMaps(defEnv, n.Cfg.Env)` — env merges with user's env taking precedence, then `n.Cfg.Env[portSpeedsEnv] = speeds` overwrites regardless. Good.

However — what about `data_nic_speed` when CHR_PORT_SPEEDS contains a pair like "2:1G"? Can't happen — always overwritten. But could a user put a glob in CHR_PORT_SPEEDS... no, overwritten.

One more subtle thing: `[ "${_pair%%:*}" = "$(( $1 + 1 ))" ] && { printf ...; return; }` — under `set -u` fine. But if the loop finishes without match, prints 10000. Good.

Performance: `data_nic_speed` is O(pairs) per NIC, called per NIC → O(N·P). N ≤ 63, P ≤ 63 → trivial. The `speeds` string also recomputes. Fine.

Now check `nic_mac` and the re-plug path uses `data_nic_device`. Let me look at the replug section. Also check that `qemu_data_nic`'s per-bridge logic unchanged. Let me view the rest of the launcher focusing on replug.

But the test name "arm64-high-port" with index 32 and pciBridges 0 → want `-device virtio-net,id=nic32,netdev=d32,mac=...,speed=10000,duplex=full`. OK.

Now, the important question: `data_nic_speed` returns the default 10000 for ARM64's `virtio-net` device. Does the `virtio-net` MMIO device (not PCI) support `speed`/`duplex` properties? `virtio-net-device` — the properties `speed` and `duplex`... Let me think. In QEMU, `virtio_net_properties` (hw/net/virtio-net.c) defines:

```c
DEFINE_PROP_UINT32("speed", VirtIONet, host_speed, 0),
DEFINE_PROP_STRING("duplex", VirtIONet, duplex_str),
```

Hmm, actually I believe speed/duplex are properties of VirtIONet (the common device core), so both `virtio-net-pci` and `virtio-net-device` (MMIO) support them. They were added in QEMU commit 93f57a3f2e ("virtio-net: add speed and duplex")... Actually I recall the commit "net: Add virtio-net... set link speed and duplex" by... it's `hw/net/virtio-net.c` DEFINE_PROP on VirtIONet. Yes — properties registered via `virtio_net_properties` used by both instance types. I'm fairly confident it applies to both. Also `-device virtio-net,id=nic$1` on ARM64 — the launcher passes `virtio-net` (alias resolved by the machine's default bus transport, virtio-mmio on ARM virt). The properties live on VirtIONet, so fine.

Does the image's QEMU version support speed/duplex? speed/duplex added in QEMU 5.0? Hmm. The property "speed" — I recall `virtio-net` gained `speed`/`duplex` in QEMU 2.7? There was a patch by Yuri Bendit... no wait. There is a known QEMU feature: `-device virtio-net-pci,speed=10000,duplex=full` documented in QEMU docs for "set the link speed and duplex as reported by the guest". It exists since 2011? Hmm. virtio-net speed/duplex: commit b8203dee (by Stefan Hajnoczi? "virtio-net: add vlan..."). I recall docs: "virtio-net-pci supports speed and duplex properties since QEMU 6.0"? Let me actually remember: qemu-options or net docs: `speed` and `duplex` are properties of virtio-net-device (i.e., common). They were added in QEMU 6.0? I think commit "net: use fallback for... virtio: add speed/duplex props" was added 2021 (QEMU 6.0) — Vincent Whitchurch? Hmm. There was a series by "Ning Bo"? I genuinely can't pin the version. The mikrotik/chr image ships a fairly recent Alpine qemu (likely 8.x/9.x). Given the test only checks the string, not QEMU behavior, and docs claim testing was done on AMD64 — the PR author presumably verified. I can't demonstrate a defect; this is a runtime question I can't verify from source. Not a finding — no evidence.

196: 			goarch:  "arm64",
197: 			ifaces:  []string{"ether31"},
198: 			wantErr: true,
199: 			errText: `interface "ether31" (eth30) exceeds the maximum data NIC index 29 on arm64 (eth29 / ether30)`,
200: 		},
201: 	}
202: 
203: 	for name, tc := range tests {
204: 		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
205: 			n := newInitialized(t, &clabtypes.NodeConfig{ShortName: "r1", LabDir: t.TempDir()})
206: 			n.goarch = "amd64"
207: 			if tc.goarch != "" {
208: 				n.goarch = tc.goarch
209: 			}
210: 
211: 			var err error
212: 			for _, ifName := range tc.ifaces {
213: 				ep := &clablinks.EndpointVeth{
214: 					EndpointGeneric: clablinks.EndpointGeneric{IfaceName: ifName},
215: 				}
216: 				if err = n.AddEndpoint(ep); err != nil {
217: 					break
218: 				}
219: 			}
220: 			if err == nil {
221: 				err = n.CheckInterfaceName()
222: 			}
223: 
224: 			if tc.wantErr {
225: 				if err == nil {
226: 					t.Fatalf("interfaces %v: want an error, got none", tc.ifaces)
227: 				}
228: 				if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.errText) {
229: 					t.Errorf(
230: 						"interfaces %v: error %q, want it to contain %q",
231: 						tc.ifaces,
232: 						err,
233: 						tc.errText,
234: 					)
235: 				}
236: 				return
237: 			}
238: 			if err != nil {
239: 				t.Fatalf("interfaces %v: %v", tc.ifaces, err)
240: 			}
241: 			for i, ep := range n.Endpoints {
242: 				if ep.GetIfaceName() != tc.want[i] {
243: 					t.Errorf(
244: 						"%q mapped to %q, want %q",
245: 						tc.ifaces[i],
246: 						ep.GetIfaceName(),
247: 						tc.want[i],
248: 					)
249: 				}
250: 			}
251: 		})
252: 	}
253: }

303: 	got := filterLauncherConfig(exportedConfig)

362: func TestFilterLauncherConfigEscapedBackslash(t *testing.T) {
363: 	// A value ending in a literal backslash is exported as `\\`: that line is complete and
364: 	// must not swallow the launcher line after it.
365: 	in := "/ip address\n" +
366: 		"add address=10.9.9.1/24 interface=ether2 network=10.9.9.0 comment=path\\\\\n" +
367: 		"add address=172.20.20.3/24 comment=clab-mgmt interface=ether1 network=\\\n" +
368: 		"    172.20.20.0\n"
369: 
370: 	got := filterLauncherConfig(in)
371: 
372: 	if !strings.Contains(
373: 		got,
374: 		"add address=10.9.9.1/24 interface=ether2 network=10.9.9.0 comment=path",
375: 	) {
376: 		t.Errorf("user address ending in an escaped backslash was dropped:\n%s", got)
377: 	}
378: 	if strings.Contains(got, "clab-mgmt") {
379: 		t.Errorf("launcher address kept:\n%s", got)
380: 	}
381: }

383: func TestContinues(t *testing.T) {
384: 	for line, want := range map[string]bool{
385: 		`add a=b`:     false,
386: 		`add a=b \`:   true,
387: 		`add a=b\\`:   false,
388: 		`add a=b\\ \`: true,
389: 		`add a=b\\\`:  true,
390: 		`add a=b\\\\`: false,
391: 	} {
392: 		if got := continues(line); got != want {
393: 			t.Errorf("continues(%q) = %v, want %v", line, got, want)
394: 		}
395: 	}
396: }

427: func TestFilterLauncherConfigDefaultKeymatProvider(t *testing.T) {
428: 	// Verbatim from a second /export on an otherwise unconfigured CHR 7.24.5.
429: 	placeholder := "add disabled=yes key-size=0 name=default qkd-cache-size=0 qkd-certificate=*0 \\\n    type=qkd"
430: 	userProvider := "add disabled=yes name=custom type=qkd"
431: 	configuredDefault := "add disabled=yes key-size=0 name=default qkd-address=192.0.2.1 qkd-cache-size=0 qkd-certificate=*0 type=qkd"
432: 	cases := []struct {
433: 		name  string
434: 		entry string
435: 		want  string
436: 	}{
437: 		{
438: 			name:  "empty factory placeholder",
439: 			entry: placeholder,
440: 			want:  "",
441: 		},
442: 		{
443: 			name:  "unfinished custom provider continuation",
444: 			entry: userProvider + ` \`,
445: 			want:  "/system keymat-provider\n" + userProvider + ` \`,
446: 		},
447: 		{
448: 			name:  "custom provider",
449: 			entry: userProvider,
450: 			want:  "/system keymat-provider\n" + userProvider,
451: 		},
452: 		{
453: 			name:  "configured default provider",
454: 			entry: configuredDefault,
455: 			want:  "/system keymat-provider\n" + configuredDefault,
456: 		},
457: 	}
458: 	for _, tc := range cases {
459: 		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
460: 			got := filterLauncherConfig("/system keymat-provider\n" + tc.entry)
461: 			if diff := cmp.Diff(tc.want, got); diff != "" {
462: 				t.Errorf("filterLauncherConfig() mismatch (-want +got):\n%s", diff)
463: 			}
464: 		})
465: 	}
466: }

Reasoning
OK — defEnv is always non-nil, so `n.Cfg.Env` is non-nil after the merge in `Init` (defEnv has USERNAME/PASSWORD). Fine; `n.Cfg.Env[portSpeedsEnv] = speeds` can't panic on nil map.

But — `Init` calls `portSpeeds(n.kindSpecificCfg(), ...)` — `kindSpecificCfg` calls `kindSpecificConfig.Of(n.Cfg)`. If `n.Cfg.KindSpecificConfig` is nil, Of sets a default. Good. If it's `*InvalidKindSpecificConfig`... when would Init be called with that? During redeploy from state? Let me check how nodes are created during redeploy — does the state file's KindSpecificConfig get reused into NodeConfig and Init called? ComputeDiff mention. Let me check where InvalidKindSpecificConfig is used.

28: 	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
29: 	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
30: 	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
31: 	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
32: )
33: 
34: var (
35: 	kindNames          = []string{"mikrotik_chr"}
36: 	defaultCredentials = clabnodes.NewCredentials("admin", "admin")
37: 
38: 	InterfaceRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`ether(?P<port>\d+)`)
39: 	InterfaceOffset = 2
40: 	InterfaceHelp   = "etherX (where X >= 2) or ethX (where X >= 1)"
41: 
42: 	//go:embed chr-launch.sh
43: 	launcherScript []byte
44: )
45: 
46: const (
47: 	configDirName   = "ftpboot"
48: 	startupCfgFName = "config.auto.rsc"
49: 
50: 	launcherFName = "chr-launch.sh"
51: 	launcherPath  = "/chr-launch.sh"
52: 
53: 	// readyFile is written by the launcher once RouterOS accepted the credentials and the
54: 	// startup config, and removed at every container start.
55: 	readyFile = "/.chr-launch-ready"
56: 
57: 	// mgmtComment tags every management object the launcher creates in RouterOS.
58: 	mgmtComment = "clab-mgmt"
59: 
60: 	// amd64's tested PCI-bridge layout. Beyond it the guest runs out of interrupt
61: 	// vectors (about 100 NICs per vCPU) and SeaBIOS out of PCI I/O space (8 bridges).
62: 	maxDataNICIndex = 63
63: 	// arm64's virt machine gets no PCI bridges: its single bus holds the disk, the
64: 	// management NIC and at most 29 data NICs before QEMU runs out of slots.
65: 	maxDataNICIndexARM64 = 29
66: 
67: 	// the launcher's CHR_INTF_WAIT and CHR_BOOT_WAIT defaults, and the time its config
68: 	// fetch and gateway check add, in seconds.
69: 	defaultIntfWait  = 60
70: 	defaultBootWait  = 300
71: 	startPeriodSlack = 90
72: 	// the launcher's wait for the interface list to settle and its re-plug rounds, in seconds.
73: 	replugWait = 180
74: 
75: 	scrapliPlatformName = "mikrotik_routeros" //nolint: misspell
76: )
77: 
78: // Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
79: func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
80: 	platformAttrs := &clabnodes.PlatformAttrs{
81: 		ScrapliPlatformName: scrapliPlatformName,
82: 	}
83: 
84: 	nrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(defaultCredentials, nil, platformAttrs).
85: 		WithKindSpecificConfig(kindSpecificConfig)
86: 
87: 	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
88: 		return new(mikrotikCHR)
89: 	}, nrea)
90: }
91: 
92: type mikrotikCHR struct {
93: 	clabnodes.VRNode
94: 	// goarch selects the NIC layout the interface limit is checked against. The
95: 	// containerlab binary's architecture matches the image's outside emulated setups.
96: 	goarch string
97: }
98: 
99: func (n *mikrotikCHR) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
100: 	n.VRNode = *clabnodes.NewVRNode(n, defaultCredentials, scrapliPlatformName)
101: 	n.ConfigDirName = configDirName
102: 	n.StartupCfgFName = startupCfgFName
103: 	// The image's qemu falls back to TCG emulation without /dev/kvm: KVM makes the boot
104: 	// fast but is not required.
105: 	n.HostRequirements.VirtRequired = false
106: 
107: 	n.Cfg = cfg
108: 	for _, o := range opts {
109: 		o(n)
110: 	}
111: 
112: 	// Credentials travel as env, not on the command line, so a password needs no quoting.
113: 	defEnv := map[string]string{
114: 		"USERNAME": n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
115: 		"PASSWORD": n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
116: 	}
117: 	n.Cfg.Env = clabutils.MergeStringMaps(defEnv, n.Cfg.Env)
118: 
119: 	n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds,
120: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, configDirName), ":/ftpboot"),
121: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName), ":", launcherPath, ":ro"),
122: 	)
123: 
124: 	if n.Cfg.Entrypoint == "" {
125: 		n.Cfg.Entrypoint = "/bin/sh " + launcherPath
126: 	}
127: 	n.Cfg.Cmd = fmt.Sprintf("--hostname %s", n.Cfg.ShortName)
128: 
129: 	if n.Cfg.Healthcheck == nil {
130: 		n.Cfg.Healthcheck = &clabtypes.HealthcheckConfig{
131: 			Test:        []string{"CMD-SHELL", "test -f " + readyFile},
132: 			Interval:    5,
133: 			Timeout:     3,
134: 			Retries:     3,
135: 			StartPeriod: startPeriod(n.Cfg.Env),
136: 		}
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	n.InterfaceRegexp = InterfaceRegexp
140: 	n.InterfaceOffset = InterfaceOffset
141: 	n.InterfaceHelp = InterfaceHelp
142: 	n.goarch = runtime.GOARCH
143: 
144: 	speeds, err := portSpeeds(n.kindSpecificCfg(), dataNICLimit(n.goarch)+1)
145: 	if err != nil {
146: 		return err
147: 	}
148: 	n.Cfg.Env[portSpeedsEnv] = speeds
149: 
150: 	return nil
151: }
152: 
153: // kindSpecificCfg returns the node's kind-specific config (port-speeds).
154: func (n *mikrotikCHR) kindSpecificCfg() *KindSpecificConfig {
155: 	return kindSpecificConfig.Of(n.Cfg)
156: }
157: 
158: // dataNICLimit is the highest data NIC index the launcher's NIC layout holds on goarch.
159: func dataNICLimit(goarch string) int {
160: 	if goarch == "arm64" {
161: 		return maxDataNICIndexARM64
162: 	}
163: 
164: 	return maxDataNICIndex
165: }
166: 
167: // CheckInterfaceName rejects data NIC indices the launcher does not create: beyond the
168: // tested PCI-bridge layout on amd64, or the free PCI slots on arm64.
169: func (n *mikrotikCHR) CheckInterfaceName() error {
170: 	if err := n.VRNode.CheckInterfaceName(); err != nil {
171: 		return err
172: 	}
173: 
174: 	limit := dataNICLimit(n.goarch)
175: 	for _, ep := range n.Endpoints {
176: 		ifName := ep.GetIfaceName()
177: 		// Name the interface as written in the topology (etherN), with its ethN mapping.
178: 		shown := fmt.Sprintf("%q", ep.GetIfaceDisplayName())
179: 		if ep.GetIfaceDisplayName() != ifName {
180: 			shown += " (" + ifName + ")"
181: 		}
182: 		index, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(ifName, "eth"))
183: 		// An index too large for an int is still an index over the limit.
184: 		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, strconv.ErrRange) {
185: 			return fmt.Errorf(
186: 				"node %q interface %s: cannot parse interface index: %w",
187: 				n.Cfg.ShortName, shown, err,
188: 			)
189: 		}
190: 		if err != nil || index > limit {
191: 			return fmt.Errorf(
192: 				"node %q interface %s exceeds the maximum data NIC index %d on %s (eth%d / ether%d)",
193: 				n.Cfg.ShortName,
194: 				shown,
195: 				limit,
196: 				n.goarch,
197: 				limit,
198: 				limit+1,
199: 			)
200: 		}
201: 	}
202: 
203: 	return nil
204: }
205: 
206: // startPeriod is the healthcheck start period in seconds: the launcher's own worst case
207: // before the ready file, so a slow boot (TCG) never reports unhealthy. It waits up to
208: // CHR_INTF_WAIT for the links, then up to CHR_BOOT_WAIT each for REST, the VRF
209: // handoff, the startup-config import and the SSH banner, plus fetch and gateway checks
210: // and re-plugging NICs RouterOS rejected.
211: func startPeriod(env map[string]string) int {
212: 	return envSeconds(env, "CHR_INTF_WAIT", defaultIntfWait) +
213: 		4*envSeconds(env, "CHR_BOOT_WAIT", defaultBootWait) + startPeriodSlack + replugWait
214: }
215: 
216: // envSeconds reads a positive number of seconds from env, else returns def (the launcher
217: // falls back to its default the same way).
218: func envSeconds(env map[string]string, key string, def int) int {
219: 	if v, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(env[key])); err == nil && v > 0 {
220: 		return v
221: 	}
222: 
223: 	return def
224: }
225: 
226: // PreDeploy writes the launcher next to the startup config on every deploy, so a
227: // containerlab upgrade ships its launcher to existing labs.
228: func (n *mikrotikCHR) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {
229: 	if err := n.VRNode.PreDeploy(ctx, params); err != nil {
230: 		return err
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	dst := filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, launcherFName)
234: 	if err := os.WriteFile(dst, launcherScript, clabconstants.PermissionsFileDefault); err != nil {
235: 		return fmt.Errorf("node %q: failed to write %s: %w", n.Cfg.ShortName, dst, err)
236: 	}
237: 
238: 	return nil
239: }
240: 
241: // PreStop skips VRNode's vrnetlab qcow2 alias step, which does not apply to this image.
242: func (*mikrotikCHR) PreStop(_ context.Context) error {
243: 	return nil
244: }
245: 
246: // SaveConfig exports the RouterOS configuration over SSH (scrapligo has no RouterOS
247: // platform, see clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH) and writes it as the node's startup config,
248: // without the objects the launcher creates at every boot. Explicit discovery=static
249: // and vrf=main settings retain user choices that compact export omits as defaults,
250: // without adding unrelated verbose defaults that older RouterOS may not understand.
251: func (n *mikrotikCHR) SaveConfig(ctx context.Context) (*clabnodes.SaveConfigResult, error) {
252: 	exported, err := clabnodes.ExportConfigOverSSH(
253: 		net.JoinHostPort(n.Cfg.LongName, "22"),
254: 		n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
255: 		n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
256: 		`/export; :if ([/ip neighbor discovery-settings get discover-interface-list] = "static") `+
257: 			`do={:put "/ip neighbor discovery-settings set discover-interface-list=static"}; `+
258: 			`:foreach s in=[/ip service find where dynamic=no vrf=main] do={`+
259: 			`:put ("/ip service set [find where name=" . [/ip service get $s name] . " dynamic=no] vrf=main")}; `+
260: 			`:if ([/snmp get vrf] = "main") do={:put "/snmp set vrf=main"}`,
261: 	)
262: 	if err != nil {
263: 		return nil, err
264: 	}
265: 
266: 	return clabnodes.WriteSavedConfig(ctx, n.Cfg, n.ConfigDirName, n.StartupCfgFName,
267: 		[]byte(filterLauncherConfig(exported)+"\n"))
268: }
269: 
270: // filterLauncherConfig drops what the launcher configures at every boot from an /export:
271: // every object tagged clab-mgmt (the ether1 management addresses, the mgmt VRF,
272: // its default routes and the discovery lists), the ether1 ND entry and CHR's ether1
273: // DHCP client. Imported again as a startup config, these lines duplicate objects the
274: // launcher already created and RouterOS stops the import at the first one; management addressing
275: // belongs to
276: // the deployment, not the lab. Continuation lines (an unescaped trailing backslash) are joined
277: // before matching.
278: func filterLauncherConfig(config string) string {
279: 	var out []string
280: 
281: 	section := ""
282: 	pending := ""
283: 	keymatHeader := ""
284: 	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.ReplaceAll(config, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n") {
285: 		if pending != "" {
286: 			line = pending + "\n" + line
287: 			pending = ""
288: 		}
289: 		if continues(line) {
290: 			pending = line
291: 			continue
292: 		}
293: 
294: 		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
295: 		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "/") {
296: 			section = trimmed
297: 			keymatHeader = ""
298: 			// Older RouterOS releases reject even an empty keymat menu. Emit
299: 			// its header only if a command remains after filtering below.
300: 			if section == "/system keymat-provider" {
301: 				keymatHeader = line
302: 				continue
303: 			}
304: 		}
305: 		if launcherOwned(section, trimmed) {
306: 			continue
307: 		}
308: 		// Repeated RouterOS exports can include this disabled factory QKD
309: 		// placeholder. Fresh imports reject it (duplicate name or empty KME
310: 		// address). Drop only this exact entry; keep configured providers.
311: 		if section == "/system keymat-provider" &&
312: 			strings.Join(strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(trimmed, `\`, "")), " ") ==
313: 				"add disabled=yes key-size=0 name=default qkd-cache-size=0 qkd-certificate=*0 type=qkd" {
314: 			continue
315: 		}
316: 		if keymatHeader != "" && trimmed != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
317: 			out = append(out, keymatHeader)
318: 			keymatHeader = ""
319: 		}
320: 		out = append(out, line)
321: 	}
322: 	if pending != "" {
323: 		if keymatHeader != "" {
324: 			out = append(out, keymatHeader)
325: 		}
326: 		out = append(out, pending)
327: 	}
328: 
329: 	return strings.Join(out, "\n")
330: }
331: 
332: // continues reports whether an /export line continues on the next one: it ends in an
333: // unescaped backslash. RouterOS writes a literal backslash in a value as `\\`, so an even
334: // run of trailing backslashes ends the line.
335: func continues(line string) bool {
336: 	trailing := len(line) - len(strings.TrimRight(line, `\`))
337: 
338: 	return trailing%2 == 1
339: }
340: 
341: func launcherOwned(section, line string) bool {
342: 	if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "add ") {
343: 		return false
344: 	}
345: 
346: 	fields := strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(line, `\`, " "))
347: 	has := func(kv string) bool { return slices.Contains(fields, kv) }
348: 
349: 	if has("comment=" + mgmtComment) {
350: 		return true
351: 	}
352: 
353: 	// /ipv6 nd keeps no comment: the launcher's ether1 entry is matched by interface.
354: 	switch section {
355: 	case "/ip address", "/ipv6 address", "/ip dhcp-client", "/ipv6 nd":
356: 		return has("interface=ether1")
357: 	}
358: 
359: 	return false
360: }

843: func configDriftReason(diff *clabtypes.TopologyDiff) string {
844: 	if diff == nil || len(diff.Fields) == 0 {
845: 		return "config drift"
846: 	}
847:

849: }

851: func (c *CLab) reconcileNodes(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) error {
852: 	if plan == nil || plan.currentNodes == nil {
853: 		return nil
854: 	}
855: 
856: 	for nodeName := range plan.currentNodes {
857: 		node, exists := c.Nodes[nodeName]
858: 		if !exists {
859: 			continue
860: 		}
861: 		if _, added := plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName]; added {
862: 			continue
863: 		}
864: 		if plan.isRootNamespaceNode(nodeName) {
865: 			continue
866: 		}
867: 		// Recreated nodes are handled exclusively by the apply pipeline
868: 		// (park -> delete -> deploy -> restore). Calling Reconcile here would
869: 		// delete the container before parkRecreatedNodes can capture its
870: 		// interfaces, breaking the recreate flow.
871: 		if _, recreated := plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName]; recreated {
872: 			continue
873: 		}
874: 
875: 		diff := plan.nodeDiffs[nodeName]
876: 
877: 		result, err := node.Reconcile(ctx, diff)
878: 		if err != nil {
879: 			return fmt.Errorf("reconcile failed for node %q: %w", nodeName, err)
880: 		}
881: 
882: 		if result.Action == clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionRestart {
883: 			if err := c.waitNodeRunning(ctx, node); err != nil {
884: 				return err
885: 			}
886: 			if err := c.waitNodeHealthyIfAvailable(ctx, node); err != nil {
887: 				return err
888: 			}
889: 		}
890: 	}
891: 
892: 	return nil
893: }

895: func (p *applyPlan) linkNeedsDeploy(link clablinks.Link) bool {
896: 	for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link) {
897: 		key := endpointKeyFromEndpoint(ep)
898: 		if _, parked := p.parkedNodeSet[key.node]; !parked {
899: 			if _, added := p.addedNodeSet[key.node]; added {
900: 				return true
901: 			}
902: 		}
903: 		if _, live := p.liveEndpointSet[key]; !live {
904: 			return true
905: 		}
906: 	}
907: 
908: 	return !p.linkIntact(link)
909: }

911: func (p *applyPlan) linkIntact(link clablinks.Link) bool {
912: 	endpoints := clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link)
913: 	if len(endpoints) != 2 || len(p.liveEndpointInfo) == 0 {
914: 		return true
915: 	}
916: 
917: 	left, leftOK := p.liveEndpointInfo[endpointKeyFromEndpoint(endpoints[0])]
918: 	right, rightOK := p.liveEndpointInfo[endpointKeyFromEndpoint(endpoints[1])]
919: 	if !leftOK || !rightOK {
920: 		return false
921: 	}
922: 
923: 	if bridgeMasterMismatch(endpoints[0], left) || bridgeMasterMismatch(endpoints[1], right) {
924: 		return false
925: 	}
926: 
927: 	return left.PeerIndex != 0 &&
928: 		right.PeerIndex != 0 &&
929: 		left.PeerIndex == right.Index &&
930: 		right.PeerIndex == left.Index
931: }
932: 
933: // bridgeMasterMismatch reports whether the live interface of a bridge endpoint is
934: // attached to a bridge other than the one the endpoint resolves to, e.g. after a
935: // mgmt-net link moved to another management network. mgmt-net endpoints whose
936: // management network bridge is not resolved are not checked.
937: func bridgeMasterMismatch(ep clablinks.Endpoint, live clablinks.OwnedInterface) bool {
938: 	node := ep.GetNode()
939: 	if node.GetLinkEndpointType() != clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridge ||
940: 		clablinks.IsUnresolvedMgmtBridgeEndpoint(ep) {
941: 		return false
942: 	}
943: 
944: 	return live.MasterName != node.GetShortName()
945: }

947: func (p *applyPlan) deployNodeNames() []string {
948: 	if p == nil {
949: 		return nil
950: 	}
951: 
952: 	nodeNames := make([]string, 0, len(p.addedNodeSet)+len(p.recreatedNodeSet))
953: 
954: 	for nodeName := range p.addedNodeSet {
955: 		nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
956: 	}
957: 	for nodeName := range p.recreatedNodeSet {
958: 		if _, added := p.addedNodeSet[nodeName]; !added {
959: 			nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
960: 		}
961: 	}
962: 
963: 	sort.Strings(nodeNames)
964: 	return nodeNames
965: }

974: 			if ref.bestEffort && errors.Is(err, clablinks.ErrInterfaceUnowned) {
975: 				log.FromContext(ctx).Debugf("skipping best-effort endpoint delete: %v", err)
976: 				continue
977: 			}
978: 			return err
979: 		}
980: 	}
981: 
982: 	return nil
983: }

<content>
1: BIN_DIR = $(CURDIR)/bin
2: BINARY = $(BIN_DIR)/containerlab
3: 
4: DATE := $(shell date)
5: COMMIT_HASH := $(shell git rev-parse --short HEAD)
6: 
7: LDFLAGS := -s -w -X 'github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/cmd.Version=0.0.0' -X 'github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/cmd.commit=$(COMMIT_HASH)' -X 'github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/cmd.date=$(DATE)'
8: PODMAN_GO_TAGS := podman exclude_graphdriver_btrfs btrfs_noversion exclude_graphdriver_devicemapper exclude_graphdriver_overlay containers_image_openpgp
9: 
10: # uv version downloaded by `install-uv` when uv is not found on the system.
11: # Keep in sync with UV_VER in .github/workflows/*.
12: UV_VERSION ?= 0.11.23
13: 
14: # Local directory used for downloaded tooling (uv). Already gitignored.
15: TOOLS_BIN_DIR ?= $(BIN_DIR)
16: 
17: # OS / arch detection used to download the matching uv release.
18: OS := $(shell uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
19: ARCH_QUERY := $(shell uname -m)
20: ifeq ($(ARCH_QUERY),x86_64)
21: ARCH := x86_64
22: else ifeq ($(ARCH_QUERY),amd64)
23: ARCH := x86_64
24: else ifeq ($(ARCH_QUERY),aarch64)
25: ARCH := aarch64
26: else ifeq ($(ARCH_QUERY),arm64)
27: ARCH := aarch64
28: else
29: ARCH := $(ARCH_QUERY)
30: endif
31: 
32: # uv ships its release binaries named after Rust target triples.
33: ifeq ($(OS),darwin)
34: UV_TARGET := $(ARCH)-apple-darwin
35: else
36: UV_TARGET := $(ARCH)-unknown-linux-gnu
37: endif
38: UV_URL := https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/download/$(UV_VERSION)/uv-$(UV_TARGET).tar.gz
39: 
40: # Prefer a uv already on PATH, otherwise fall back to the locally downloaded
41: # copy that `install-uv` places in TOOLS_BIN_DIR.
42: UV := $(shell command -v uv 2>/dev/null)
43: ifeq ($(UV),)
44: UV := $(TOOLS_BIN_DIR)/uv
45: endif
46: 
47: include .mk/lint.mk
48: 
49: all: build
50: 
51: build:
52: 	mkdir -p $(BIN_DIR)
53: 	CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o $(BINARY) -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" main.go
54: 	sudo chown root:root $(BINARY)
55: 	sudo chmod 4755 $(BINARY)
56: 
57: build-linux-arm64:
58: 	mkdir -p $(BIN_DIR)
59: 	GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 go build -o $(BINARY) -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" main.go
60: 	sudo chown root:root $(BINARY)
61: 	sudo chmod 4755 $(BINARY)
62: 
63: build-linux-amd64:
64: 	mkdir -p $(BIN_DIR)
65: 	GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -o $(BINARY) -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" main.go
66: 	sudo chown root:root $(BINARY)
67: 	sudo chmod 4755 $(BINARY)
68: 
69: build-with-cover:
70: 	mkdir -p $(BIN_DIR)
71: 	go build -cover -o $(BINARY) -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" main.go
72: 	sudo chown root:root $(BINARY)
73: 	sudo chmod 4755 $(BINARY)
74: 
75: build-debug:
76: 	mkdir -p $(BIN_DIR)
77: 	CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -o $(BINARY) -gcflags=all="-N -l" -race -cover main.go
78: 	sudo chown root:root $(BINARY)
79: 	sudo chmod 4755 $(BINARY)
80: 
81: build-dlv-debug:
82: 	mkdir -p $(BIN_DIR)
83: 	go build -o $(BINARY) -gcflags=all="-N -l" main.go
84: 	sudo chown root:root $(BINARY)
85: 	sudo chmod 4755 $(BINARY)
86: 
87: 
88: build-with-podman:
89: 	mkdir -p $(BIN_DIR)
90: 	CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o $(BINARY) -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" -trimpath -tags "$(PODMAN_GO_TAGS)" main.go
91: 	chmod a+x $(BINARY)
92: 	sudo chown root:root $(BINARY)
93: 	sudo chmod 4755 $(BINARY)
94: 
95: build-with-podman-debug:
96: 	mkdir -p $(BIN_DIR)
97: 	CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -o $(BINARY) -gcflags=all="-N -l" -race -cover -trimpath -tags "$(PODMAN_GO_TAGS)" main.go
98: 	sudo chown root:root $(BINARY)
99: 	sudo chmod 4755 $(BINARY)
100: 
101: convert-coverage:
102: 	go tool covdata textfmt -i=/tmp/clab-tests/coverage -o coverage.out
103: 
104: test:
105: 	rm -rf /tmp/clab-tests/coverage
106: 	mkdir -p /tmp/clab-tests/coverage
107: 	CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -cover -race ./... -v -covermode atomic -args -test.gocoverdir="/tmp/clab-tests/coverage"
108: 
109: 
110: ifndef runtime
111: override runtime = docker
112: endif
113: ifndef suite
114: override suite = .
115: endif
116: .PHONY: robot-test
117: robot-test: build-with-podman-debug
118: 	sudo chown root:root $(BINARY) && sudo chmod 4755 $(BINARY)
119: 	CLAB_BIN=$(BINARY) $$PWD/tests/rf-run.sh $(runtime) $$PWD/tests/$(suite)
120: 
121: MOCKDIR = ./mocks
122: .PHONY: mocks-gen
123: mocks-gen: mocks-rm ## Generate mocks for all the defined interfaces.
124: 	go install go.uber.org/mock/mockgen@latest
125: 	mockgen -package=mocknodes -source=nodes/node.go -destination=$(MOCKDIR)/mocknodes/node.go
126: 	mockgen -package=mocks -source=core/dependency_manager/dependency_manager.go -destination=$(MOCKDIR)/dependency_manager.go
127: 	mockgen -package=mockruntime -source=runtime/runtime.go -destination=$(MOCKDIR)/mockruntime/runtime.go
128: 	mockgen -package=mocknodes -source=nodes/default_node.go -destination=$(MOCKDIR)/mocknodes/default_node.go
129: 	mockgen -package=mocks -source=core/exec.go -destination=$(MOCKDIR)/exec.go
130: 
131: .PHONY: mocks-rm
132: mocks-rm: ## remove generated mocks
133: 	rm -rf $(MOCKDIR)/*
134: 
135: lint:
136: 	golangci-lint run
137: 
138: 
139: 
140: # Download uv for the detected OS/arch into TOOLS_BIN_DIR.
141: .PHONY: install-uv
142: install-uv:
143: 	@mkdir -p $(TOOLS_BIN_DIR)
144: 	@echo "--> downloading uv $(UV_VERSION) ($(UV_TARGET)) to $(TOOLS_BIN_DIR)"
145: 	@curl --location --silent --fail --show-error --output - $(UV_URL) \
146: 		| tar -xz --strip-components=1 -C $(TOOLS_BIN_DIR) uv-$(UV_TARGET)/uv uv-$(UV_TARGET)/uvx
147: 	@chmod +x $(TOOLS_BIN_DIR)/uv $(TOOLS_BIN_DIR)/uvx
148: 
149: # Ensure uv is available before running any docs target; download it if missing.
150: .PHONY: ensure-uv
151: ensure-uv:
152: 	@command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 || test -x $(TOOLS_BIN_DIR)/uv || $(MAKE) install-uv
153: 
154: .PHONY: docs
155: docs: ensure-uv
156: 	$(UV) run --group docs zensical build --clean --strict
157: 
158: .PHONY: site
159: site: ensure-uv
160: 	$(UV) run --group docs zensical serve -a 0.0.0.0:8000
161: 
162: # serve the site locally using zensical
163: .PHONY: serve-docs-full
164: serve-docs-full: ensure-uv
165: 	$(UV) run --group docs zensical serve -a 0.0.0.0:8001
166: 
167: 
168: # serve the site locally using zensical
169: # zensical performs incremental rebuilds, so content and navigation update automatically.
170: .PHONY: serve-docs
171: serve-docs: ensure-uv
172: 	$(UV) run --group docs zensical serve -a 0.0.0.0:8001
173: 
174: .PHONY: htmltest
175: htmltest: ensure-uv
176: 	$(UV) run --group docs zensical build --clean --strict
177: 	docker run --rm -v $(CURDIR):/test wjdp/htmltest --conf ./site/htmltest-w-github.yml
178: 	rm -rf ./site

143: # ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------
144: # shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here
145: count_intfs() { ls -d "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }
146: waited=0
147: while [ "$(count_intfs)" -lt "$INTFS" ] && [ "$waited" -lt "$INTF_WAIT" ]; do
148:     sleep 1
149:     waited=$((waited + 1))
150: done
151: log "interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s"
152: 
153: # ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------
154: # The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.
155: case "$(uname -m)" in
156:     aarch64|arm64)
157:         QEMU="qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd"
158:         PCI_BRIDGES=0
159:         TCG_CPU="-cpu cortex-a57" ;;
160:     *)
161:         QEMU="qemu-system-x86_64"
162:         PCI_BRIDGES=1
163:         TCG_CPU="" ;;
164: esac
165: if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then
166:     ACCEL="-cpu host -accel kvm"
167: else
168:     ACCEL="$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on"
169:     log "no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)"
170: fi
171: 
172: # MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per
173: # node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the
174: # interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on
175: # a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST
176: # boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).
177: node_id="$(cat "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
178: case "$node_id" in
179:     [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;
180:     *)
181:         e="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/address" 2>/dev/null)"
182:         if [ -n "$e" ]; then
183:             o2="${e##*:}"; rest_mac="${e%:*}"; o1="${rest_mac##*:}"
184:             node_id="$o1:$o2"
185:         else
186:             node_id="$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 "%02x:"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')"
187:         fi
188:         printf '%s\n' "$node_id" > "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null \
189:             || log "node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs"
190:         ;;
191: esac
192: NET="-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00"
193: nic_mac() { # nic_mac <index>: the data NIC's MAC, its index in the last octet
194:     printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' "$node_id" "$1"
195: }
196: 
197: check_nic_index() { # check_nic_index <max-index>: reject indices beyond the NIC layout
198:     # 63 NICs behind bridges are tested. More run into the guest's interrupt
199:     # vectors (about 100 NICs per vCPU) and SeaBIOS's PCI I/O space (8 bridges).
200:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" = 1 ] && [ "$1" -gt 63 ]; then
201:         log "at most 63 data NICs are supported (eth63 / ether64); index $1 is beyond the tested limit"
202:         return 1
203:     fi
204:     # Without bridges (arm64 virt) one bus holds the disk, management and 29 data NICs.
205:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" != 1 ] && [ "$1" -gt 29 ]; then
206:         log "at most 29 data NICs fit without PCI bridges (eth29 / ether30); index $1 leaves no PCI slot for the disk"
207:         return 1
208:     fi
209: }
210: 
211: data_nic_speed() { # data_nic_speed <index>: the data NIC's speed in Mb/s
212:     # The kind writes the validated port-speeds key to CHR_PORT_SPEEDS as
213:     # "<port>:<Mb/s>" pairs; data NIC <index> is ether<index+1>. Other ports
214:     # report 10G, the speed a container veth reports.
215:     for _pair in ${CHR_PORT_SPEEDS:-}; do
216:         [ "${_pair%%:*}" = "$(( $1 + 1 ))" ] && { printf '%s' "${_pair#*:}"; return; }
217:     done
218:     printf '%s' 10000
219: }
220: 
221: data_nic_device() { # data_nic_device <index> <mac>: the NIC's -device value (also used to re-plug it)
222:     # A virtio NIC reports no speed and half duplex unless told otherwise, and
223:     # RouterOS bonds in 802.3ad mode only with full-duplex ports.
224:     _link="speed=$(data_nic_speed "$1"),duplex=full"
225:     case "$PCI_BRIDGES" in
226:         1)
227:             # The default PC has only 29 free PCI slots, including management.
228:             # Keep management on the root bus and put data NICs behind bridges.
229:             # Follow vrnetlab's conservative allocation of 25 NICs per bridge.
230:             # Omit PXE ROMs to avoid exhausting SeaBIOS option-ROM space.
231:             # Keep MSI-X, but share one vector between RX/TX queues (plus one
232:             # for config) to reduce IRQ pressure.
233:             # Disabling MSI-X entirely can leave NICs missing in RouterOS.
234:             printf '%s' "virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2,bus=chrpci$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 )),addr=$(printf '0x%x' $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 + 1 ))),romfile=,vectors=2,$_link"
235:             ;;
236:         *)
237:             # ARM64 uses the virt machine and keeps its existing NIC layout.
238:             printf '%s' "virtio-net,id=nic$1,netdev=d$1,mac=$2,$_link"
239:             ;;
240:     esac
241: }
242: 
243: qemu_data_nic() { # qemu_data_nic <index> <mac>: append-only QEMU arguments
244:     # Each bridge comes right before its first NIC.
245:     if [ "$PCI_BRIDGES" = 1 ] && [ $(( ($1 - 1) % 25 )) -eq 0 ]; then
246:         _bridge=$(( ($1 - 1) / 25 + 1 ))
247:         printf '%s ' "-device pci-bridge,id=chrpci$_bridge,chassis_nr=$_bridge,bus=pci.0"
248:     fi
249:     printf '%s' "-netdev tap,id=d$1,ifname=tap$1,script=no,downscript=no -device $(data_nic_device "$1" "$2")"
250: }
251: 
252: # ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----
253: ip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix
254:     ip -"$1" addr show dev "$2" 2>/dev/null \
255:         | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\{0,1\} \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
256: }
257: ip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway
258:     ip -"$1" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
259: }
260: M4="$(ip_global 4 eth0)"; M6="$(ip_global 6 eth0)"
261: G4="$(ip_gw 4)"; G6="$(ip_gw 6)"
262: if [ -n "$M4$M6" ]; then
263:     printf 'M4=%s\nM6=%s\nG4=%s\nG6=%s\n' "$M4" "$M6" "$G4" "$G6" > "$MGMT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
264: elif [ -f "$MGMT_FILE" ]; then
265:     # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments
266:     . "$MGMT_FILE"
267: fi
268: log "management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}"
269:

Reasoning
`data_nic_speed` looks correct:
- `for _pair in ${CHR_PORT_SPEEDS:-}` — unquoted expansion is intentional word splitting; values are validated by the kind (port numbers and speeds, no glob chars possible: `port` is validated as digits via `strconv.Itoa(first) != firstText` etc., speed is an int 1..MaxInt32 — no glob metacharacters can appear). Wait — could a user-set `env CHR_PORT_SPEEDS` reach the launcher with glob chars? No — Init always overwrites it with the validated value (test "replaces-env" covers). But the launcher can also run standalone (the entrypoint is overridable? `n.Cfg.Entrypoint` user-set → user could set entrypoint... but then they wouldn't run chr-launch.sh). Edge case negligible.

- `${_pair%%:*}` strips from last `:` — wait, `%%` strips the longest suffix matching `:*`. For "2:1000", `${_pair%%:*}` = "2" (longest suffix from the first `:`). Yes = "2". `${_pair#*:}` = shortest prefix strip → "1000". Good.
- Comparison `[ "2" = "$(( $1 + 1 ))" ]` — string compare, no prefix issue ("12" vs "1"? no: equality). Test "no-prefix-match" covers.
- `$(( $1 + 1 ))` — $1 is the eth index (0-based? data NIC index 1-based). data NIC index N = ether(N+1). In test: index 1 → matches "2:1000". Good.

`data_nic_device` appends `speed=...,duplex=full` — this is the change to the device string. Previously (base) presumably no `speed=` at all. The `TestQEMUDataNIC` expectations were updated with `speed=10000,duplex=full`.

Now — the important performance/behavioral check: `data_nic_speed` is called inside `data_nic_device`, which is called once per NIC at startup (63 max) and once per re-plug. Each call iterates CHR_PORT_SPEEDS pairs (max 63). Trivial. Fine.

One subtle thing: in `data_nic_speed`, when a pair matches but `${_pair#*:}` is empty (e.g. "2:"), it would print empty speed → QEMU arg `speed=,duplex=full` → invalid. Can't happen with kind-validated input. Env always overwritten. OK.

<content>
270: tunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap
271: if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR" ]; then
272:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
273:     ip addr flush dev eth0
274:     # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the
275:     # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.
276:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null
277:     brctl addbr "$MGMT_BR"
278:     brctl setfd "$MGMT_BR" 0 2>/dev/null
279:     echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
280:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" address "52:54:01:$node_id:00"
281:     ip link set tap0 mtu "$_mtu"
282:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" mtu "$_mtu"
283:     # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until
284:     # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's
285:     # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.
286:     brctl addif "$MGMT_BR" tap0
287:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \
288:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0" "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0" \
289:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0" 2>/dev/null
290: fi
291: ip link set tap0 up
292: ip link set "$MGMT_BR" up
293: # RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it
294: VM_LL="fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00"
295: VM_EP="$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR"
296: # The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read
297: # once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and
298: # the address stays tentative.
299: LL=""
300: bridge_ll() {
301:     _w=0
302:     while [ -z "$LL" ] && [ "$_w" -lt 20 ]; do
303:         LL="$(ip -6 addr show dev "$MGMT_BR" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \
304:             | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \(fe80::[^/]*\)\/64 .*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
305:         [ -n "$LL" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }
306:     done
307:     [ -n "$LL" ] || log "no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR"
308: }
309: 
310: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk
311: # eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS
312: # numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count
313: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and
314: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the
315: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes
316: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.
317: max=0
318: for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
319:     [ -e "$d" ] || continue
320:     n="${d##*/eth}"
321:     [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] && max="$n"
322: done
323: prev="$(cat "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
324: case "$prev" in *[!0-9]*|"") prev=0 ;; esac
325: [ "$prev" -gt "$max" ] && max="$prev"
326: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after
327: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and
328: # the watcher bridges the late veths.
329: case "$INTFS" in *[!0-9]*|"") INTFS=0 ;; esac
330: [ "$INTFS" -gt "$max" ] && max="$INTFS"
331: check_nic_index "$max" || exit 1
332: [ "$max" -gt "$prev" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$max" > "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true; }
333: 
334: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system
335: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse
336: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.
337: if [ -z "${MEM:-}" ]; then
338:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))
339: fi
340: 
341: bridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)
342:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
343:     if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$1" ]; then
344:         brctl addbr "br$1"
345:         ip link set "br$1" mtu "$_mtu"
346:         ip link set "tap$1" mtu "$_mtu"
347:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14). The bridge refuses LACP
348:         # (01:80:c2:00:00:02, bit 2), so each port forwards it (below).
349:         echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
350:         brctl addif "br$1" "tap$1"
351:         echo 4 > "$SYSNET/tap$1/brport/group_fwd_mask" ||
352:             log "could not enable LACP forwarding on tap$1 (bridge br$1)"
353:     fi
354:     brctl addif "br$1" "eth$1"
355:     echo 4 > "$SYSNET/eth$1/brport/group_fwd_mask" ||
356:         log "could not enable LACP forwarding on eth$1 (bridge br$1)"
357:     ip link set "eth$1" up
358:     ip link set "br$1" up
359: }
360: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link
361: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's
362: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS
363: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.
364: watch_links() {
365:     _warned=""
366:     while kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
367:         i=1
368:         while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
369:             if [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i" ]; then
370:                 bridge_eth "$i" && log "link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i"
371:             fi
372:             i=$((i + 1))
373:         done
374:         for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
375:             [ -e "$d" ] || continue
376:             n="${d##*/eth}"
377:             [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] || continue
378:             case " $_warned " in *" $n "*) continue ;; esac
379:             _warned="$_warned $n"
380:             log "link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted"
381:         done
382:         sleep 2
383:     done
384: }
385: 
386: i=1
387: speeds=""
388: while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
389:     tap="tap$i"
390:     tunctl -t "$tap" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev "$tap" mode tap
391:     [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && bridge_eth "$i"
392:     ip link set "$tap" up
393:     NET="$NET $(qemu_data_nic "$i" "$(nic_mac "$i")")"
394:     speeds="$speeds ether$((i + 1))=$(data_nic_speed "$i")"
395:     i=$((i + 1))
396: done
397: # One line with the speed of every data NIC, so a port-speeds entry for a
398: # port this node does not create is visible here.
399: [ "$max" -gt 0 ] && log "data NIC speeds (Mb/s):$speeds"
400: 
401: # shellcheck disable=SC2086
402: $QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \
403:     -qmp "tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_PORT,server,nowait" \
404:     -qmp "tcp:127.0.0.1:$QMP_EVENT_PORT,server,nowait" \
405:     -m "$MEM" -smp "cpus=$CPUS" \
406:     -drive "file=$IMG,format=raw" \
407:     -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \
408:     $NET &
409: QEMU_PID=$!
410: trap 'kill "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT
411: log "qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)"
412: watch_links &
413: 
414: # ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
415: json_str() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g'; }
416: rest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]
417:     # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI
418:     # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the
419:     # read timeout (default 20s).
420:     _auth="Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')"
421:     if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then
422:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
423:             --header "$_auth" --post-data "$3" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
424:     else
425:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "$_auth" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
426:     fi
427: }
428: # busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts
429: # its diagnosis ONLY there ({"detail":"Script Error: … (line N column M)"}; its
430: # /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw
431: # HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,
432: # reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite
433: # `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed
434: # once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.
435: resp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived
436:     _cl="$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')"
437:     [ -n "$_cl" ] || return 1
438:     grep -q -m1 '^\r*$' "$1" 2>/dev/null || return 1
439:     [ "$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$1" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" -ge "$_cl" ]
440: }
441: rest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> "<status> <body>"
442:     _f="/tmp/chr-rest.$$"; rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"; mkfifo "$_f" || return 1
443:     timeout "$(( $4 + 5 ))" nc "$VM_EP" 80 <"$_f" >"$_f.out" 2>/dev/null &
444:     _pid=$!
445:     exec 7>"$_f"
446:     printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: [%s]\r\nAuthorization: Basic %s\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n%s' \
447:         "$2" "$VM_LL" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" \
448:         "$(printf '%s' "$3" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" "$3" >&7
449:     _left=$4
450:     while kill -0 "$_pid" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete "$_f.out" && [ "$_left" -gt 0 ]; do
451:         sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))
452:     done
453:     exec 7>&-
454:     wait "$_pid" 2>/dev/null
455:     _st="$(head -n1 "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)"
456:     _body="$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')"
457:     rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"
458:     printf '%s %s' "${_st:-000}" "$_body"
459: }
460: # RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a
461: # bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently
462: # failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.
463: is_err() { case "$1" in *'"error"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }
464: 
465: # ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------
466: waited=0
467: AUTH=""
468: # A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank
469: # password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username
470: # asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that
471: # answers is the requested user.
472: while [ -z "$AUTH" ]; do
473:     for _cred in "admin:" "admin:$PASSWORD" "$USERNAME:$PASSWORD"; do
474:         rest "$_cred" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH="$_cred"; break; }
475:     done
476:     [ -n "$AUTH" ] && break
477:     if ! kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
478:         log "qemu exited during boot"
479:         exit 1

61: diff --git a/docs/manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md b/docs/manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md
62: index 4107550..ee16698 100644
63: --- a/docs/manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md
64: +++ b/docs/manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md
65: @@ -65,28 +65,66 @@ You can use [interface names](../topo-def-file.md#interface-naming) in the topol
66:  /// admonition
67:      type: warning
68:  Data ports start at `ether2`: `ether1` is the management interface. Using `ether1` in a topology results in an error.
69:  ///
70:  
71: -The container interface `ethN` is RouterOS `ether(N+1)`, also when links leave gaps: a link on `eth12` alone still lands on `ether13`, with `ether2` to `ether12` present and unlinked. Interface MTU follows the link MTU, and LLDP frames are forwarded, so `/ip neighbor` shows the peers.
72: +The container interface `ethN` is RouterOS `ether(N+1)`, also when links leave gaps: a link on `eth12` alone still lands on `ether13`, with `ether2` to `ether12` present and unlinked. Interface MTU follows the link MTU, and LLDP and LACP frames are forwarded, so `/ip neighbor` shows the peers and 802.3ad bonds can form.
73:  
74:  On AMD64, data NICs are placed behind PCI bridges rather than sharing the default PC's root bus with all other devices. This removes the default layout's limit of 29 total Ethernet interfaces (management plus 28 data ports), so links can use `ether30` and higher without a custom launcher. ARM64 still uses a single PCI bus on the `virt` machine, shared with the disk and the management NIC; the PCI-bridge expansion applies only to AMD64.
75:  
76:  /// admonition
77:      type: warning
78: -The highest interface depends on the architecture, and larger indices are rejected during deployment:
79: +Containerlab checks the highest interface index against these architecture limits:
80:  
81:  * AMD64: `eth63` / `ether64`, the highest port tested. More interfaces exhaust the guest's interrupt vectors (with the default single vCPU) and, from about 200, the virtual PC firmware's PCI address space, which stops the VM before RouterOS boots.
82: -* ARM64: `eth29` / `ether30`, the last data port that fits on the `virt` machine's PCI bus.
83: +* ARM64: `eth29` / `ether30`, the last data port that fits on the `virt` machine's PCI bus. RouterOS may stop earlier. With QEMU software emulation (TCG), RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.26beta7 brought up only 22 data NICs, through `eth22` / `ether23`. A topology that links `ether24` or higher can pass validation but leave the node unhealthy. Keep links at or below `ether23` on these ARM64 setups.
84:  
85:  The check uses the architecture of the containerlab binary, which matches the image's except in emulated setups.
86:  ///
87:  
88:  With more than about 30 data ports, RouterOS can reject a NIC while it boots, and the interface does not appear. The launcher checks that RouterOS has an interface for every data NIC and re-plugs the missing ones before the node reports ready; RouterOS keeps their configuration. It checks again after RouterOS reboots itself (for example with `/system reboot`), when the container keeps running. If a NIC is still missing, the launcher logs `data NIC check FAILED` and the node is not healthy. The node is also not healthy while RouterOS does not answer within `CHR_BOOT_WAIT` after such a reboot.
89:  
90:  Sparse interface numbering also consumes VM resources for the intervening ports; memory defaults scale with the highest index, not just the number of links.
91:  
92: +### Port speed
93: +
94: +Data interfaces report 10 Gbit/s and full duplex by default, matching a container veth. RouterOS needs full-duplex member links for an 802.3ad bond. Each data bridge must also forward LACP frames between the container veth and the QEMU tap so RouterOS and its peer can negotiate the bond.
95: +
96: +To model the ports of a real device, set `port-speeds`, a [kind-specific config](../nodes.md#kind-specific-config) key. Each entry sets the speed in Mb/s for one data port or an inclusive range: `port` is the RouterOS port number (`2` for `ether2`) or a range such as `2..25`. Ports that are not listed keep 10 Gbit/s. The speed is what RouterOS shows; it does not limit traffic.
97: +
98: +Set `port-speeds` in a [group](../topo-def-file.md#groups) to describe a device model once and reuse it. A device's own management port is `ether1`, the node's management interface. Assign data ports starting at `ether2`. The CRS518 example puts the 25G ports first. A QSFP cage counts as one port, as RouterOS runs the full 40G or 100G link on its first lane.
99: +
100: +```yaml
101: +name: chr-port-speeds
102: +topology:
103: +  groups:
104: +    crs317-1g-16s: # 16 x 10G SFP+
105: +      kind: mikrotik_chr
106: +      image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5
107: +      port-speeds:
108: +        - port: 2..17
109: +          speed: 10000
110: +    crs518-16xs-2xq: # 16 x 25G SFP28, 2 x 100G QSFP28
111: +      kind: mikrotik_chr
112: +      image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5
113: +      port-speeds:
114: +        - port: 2..17
115: +          speed: 25000
116: +        - port: 18..19
117: +          speed: 100000
118: +  nodes:
119: +    access1:
120: +      group: crs317-1g-16s
121: +    core1:
122: +      group: crs518-16xs-2xq
123: +  links:
124: +    - endpoints: ["access1:ether16", "core1:ether2"]
125: +    - endpoints: ["access1:ether17", "core1:ether19"]
126: +```
127: +
128: +A node that sets `port-speeds` itself replaces the group's list. Use `port-speeds: []` to restore the defaults. Containerlab rejects `ether1`, a port above the [architecture limit](#interface-naming), a duplicate port, or a speed outside 1 to 2147483647 Mb/s. A group may list ports without links. The container log lists the speed of each data NIC the node creates.
129: +
130:  ## Node configuration
131:  
132:  -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes boot with the default CHR configuration plus the credentials, the identity (set to the node name) and the management setup described below.
133:  
134:  ### Startup configuration

Reasoning
Docs look thorough. One docs statement to verify: "Use `port-speeds: []` to restore the defaults." — does `port-speeds: []` in a node replace a group's list with empty? The precedence merge in `GetNodeKindSpecificConfig` collects entries per key with nodes > groups > kinds; an explicit empty list at node level replaces the group's list (first block that sets the key provides the whole value). The entry value `[]` decodes to an empty slice → `portSpeeds` returns "" → all ports 10G. Need to verify the topology merge treats an empty list as "set". `GetNodeKindSpecificConfig` in types/topology.go — I read lines 1175-1240 earlier. Let me re-verify how it decides whether a key is set — does an empty list count? If it uses reflection `!nd.KindSpecificConfig.IsZero()` style checks, an empty slice might be treated as unset and the group's list would win, contradicting the docs. Let me check.

Also the config_test.go test — the diff hunk at line 5-60 of diff.txt — covers group inheritance. Let me re-read that hunk plus check GetNodeKindSpecificConfig.
